[[5:8|And they held their peace, and found not what to answer|Et siluerunt, nec invenerunt quid responderent]]: for in this case of general affliction and want they ought to have relieved their needy neighbours freely and mercifully.

paras.t: Et dixi eis: Non est bona res quam facitis. Quare non in timore Dei nostri filiali aut saltem initiali ambulatis, custodiendo divina præcepta? quia qui timet Deum, nihil negligit; ne exprobretur nobis ab inimicis nostris, id est, ne adversariis subjiciamur, et ne nobis insultent: juxta illud, Ne dicant inter gentes, Ubi est Deus eorum? Principaliter tamen Deum timere et honorare debemus ex caritate ipsius, quatenus ei complaceamus et uniamur. Istud dicendum est Christianis, ut scilicet timeant Deum, et obediant ei, ne exprobretur eis ab hostibus eorum, Turcis et Sarracenis.
paras.en: And I said to them: [[5:9|The thing you do is not good|Non est bona res quam facitis]]. [[5:9|why walk you not in the fear of our God|Quare non in timore Dei nostri]], with a filial or at least an initial fear [filial fear is a son's fear of offending a father he loves; initial fear, that of beginners, still mixed with fear of punishment], keeping God's commandments? For [[Eccles 7:19|he that feareth God, neglecteth nothing|qui timet Deum, nihil negligit]]; [[5:9|that we be not exposed to the reproaches of the Gentiles our enemies|ne exprobretur nobis ab inimicis nostris]], that is, lest we be made subject to our adversaries, and lest they insult us: according to that, [[Ps 78:10|Lest they should say among the Gentiles: Where is their God?|Ne dicant inter gentes, Ubi est Deus eorum?]] Yet principally we ought to fear and honour God out of charity towards him, so that we may please him and be united to him. This is to be said to Christians: that they should fear God and obey him, lest they be reproached by their enemies, the Turks and Saracens.

paras.t: Deinde Nehemias exemplo sui ipsius et suorum, hortatur Judæos ad liberalitatem et pietatem prætactas. Et ego et fratres mei et pueri mei domestici, commodavimus plurimis, id est, gratis concessimus multis Judæis pauperibus, pecuniam et frumentum. Non repetamus in commune istud, id est, communiter in hoc concordemus, quod ista sic mutuata, non repetantur ab eis qui facultatem non habent solvendi. Æs alienum concedamus quod debetur nobis, id est, pecuniam quæ nobis debetur a subditis ratione nostri ducatus, non exigimus nobis persolvi, sed quasi mutuatum quid relinquimus illis. Reddite ergo eis agros suos et vineas, etc. Quin potius et centesimam pecuniæ, id est centesimam partem pecuniæ, frumenti, vini et olei, quam exigere ab eis solebatis, date pro illis, id est, solvite pro ipsis pauperibus de bonis vestris, quum ipsi non habeant unde persolvant. Hæc centesima solvebatur regi pro tributo terræ. Insuper et excussi sinum meum, et dixi: Sic excutiat Dominus omnem virum, de quo loquor, qui non compleverit verbum istud, etc.
paras.en: Then Nehemias, by the example of himself and his household, exhorts the Jews to the liberality and kindness spoken of. [[5:10|Both I and my brethren, and my servants|Et ego et fratres mei et pueri mei]] of my household [[5:10|have lent|commodavimus]] [[5:10|to many|plurimis]], that is, have freely granted to many poor Jews, [[5:10|money and corn|pecuniam et frumentum]]. [[5:10|let us all agree not to call for it again|Non repetamus in commune istud]], that is, let us agree in common on this, that what has been lent in this way should not be called back from those who have no means of paying. [[5:10|let us forgive the debt that is owing to us|Æs alienum concedamus quod debetur nobis]], that is, the money which is owing to us from our subjects by reason of our governorship we do not require to be paid to us, but leave it to them as a thing lent. [[5:11|Restore ye to them|Reddite ergo eis]] [[5:11|their fields, and their vineyards|agros suos et vineas]], etc. [[5:11|and the hundredth part of the money|Quin potius et centesimam pecuniæ]], that is, the hundredth part of the money, [[5:11|and of the corn, the wine, and the oil, which you were wont to exact of them|frumenti, vini et olei, quam exigere ab eis solebatis]], [[5:11|give it rather for them|date pro illis]], that is, pay it for these poor men out of your own goods, since they have nothing to pay it with. This hundredth was paid to the king as tribute for the land. [[5:13|Moreover I shook my lap, and said|Insuper et excussi sinum meum, et dixi]]: [[5:13|So may God shake every man|Sic excutiat Dominus omnem virum]] of whom I speak, [[5:13|that shall not accomplish this word|qui non compleverit verbum istud]], etc.

paras.t: A die autem illa qua præceperat rex mihi, ut essem dux in terra Juda, id est per duodecim annos quibus præfui populo Judæorum ut dux, ex regis commissione, ego et fratres mei annonas non comedimus, id est, victum a populo non accepi, qui tamen mihi debebatur ratione ducatus mei, si exegissem. Quin potius in opere muri ædificavi propria manu interdum, et agrum non emi, quia propria commoda et divitias non quæsivi, sed Dei honorem et bonum commune.
paras.en: [[5:14|And from the day, in which the king commanded me to be governor in the land of Juda|A die autem illa qua præceperat rex mihi, ut essem dux in terra Juda]], that is, for the twelve years in which I was over the Jewish people as governor by the king's commission, [[5:14|I and my brethren did not eat the yearly allowance|ego et fratres mei annonas non comedimus]], that is, I did not take my keep from the people, which was nevertheless due to me by reason of my governorship, had I required it. [[5:16|Moreover I built in the work of the wall|Quin potius in opere muri ædificavi]], at times with my own hand, [[5:16|and I bought no land|et agrum non emi]], because I sought not my own advantage and riches, but God's honour and the common good.

paras.t: Judæi quoque et magistratus, centum quinquaginta viri, qui in officiis erant et a populo sustentari solebant, et qui veniebant ad nos de gentibus, in mensa mea erant: et sic fui hospes liberalis, ne populus gravaretur. Parabatur mihi, id est pro esu meo et eorum quos reficere volui, per dies singulos, id est quotidie, bos unus, arietes sex, et inter dies decem vina diversa, id est, plura dolia vinorum diversorum infra decem dies expendi cum commensalibus meis. Insuper et annonas ducatus mei non quæsivi. Valde enim attenuatus, id est per paupertatem exhaustus, erat populus pro majori parte. Memento mei, Deus meus, in bonum, id est ad hoc, ut mihi misericors sis et gratiose retribuas, secundum omnia quæ feci populo huic Judæorum, id est secundum merita beneficiorum quæ eis exhibui propter te; et sicut pie et liberaliter feci eis, ita fac mecum: juxta illud, Qua mensura mensi fueritis, remetietur vobis.
paras.en: [[5:17|The Jews also and the magistrates|Judæi quoque et magistratus]], [[5:17|one hundred and fifty men|centum quinquaginta viri]], who were in office and used to be maintained by the people, [[5:17|besides them that came to us from among the nations|et qui veniebant ad nos de gentibus]], [[5:17|were at my table|in mensa mea erant]]: and so I was a liberal host, so that the people should not be burdened. [[5:18|And there was prepared for me|Parabatur mihi]], that is, for my own eating and for those whom I wished to feed, [[5:18|day be day|per dies singulos]], that is, daily, [[5:18|one ox, and six choice rams|bos unus, arietes sex]], [[5:18|and once in ten days I gave store of divers wines|et inter dies decem vina diversa]], that is, within ten days I spent many casks of divers wines with those who sat at table with me. [[5:18|yet I did not require my yearly allowance as governor|Insuper et annonas ducatus mei non quæsivi]]. [[5:18|for the people were very much impoverished|valde enim attenuatus erat populus]], that is, worn out by poverty, for the most part. [[5:19|Remember me, O my God, for good|Memento mei, Deus meus, in bonum]], that is, to this end, that thou mayest be merciful to me and graciously reward me, [[5:19|according to all that I have done for this people|secundum omnia quæ feci populo huic]] of the Jews, that is, according to the merits of the benefits which I showed them for thy sake; and as I have dealt kindly and liberally with them, so deal thou with me: according to that, [[Matt 7:2|with what measure you mete, it shall be measured to you again|Qua mensura mensi fueritis, remetietur vobis]][[Luke 6:38||]].

paras.t: Ex isto capitulo ad opera pietatis instruimur; sed heu! jam multi infelicissimi nomine tenus Christiani, Judæorum avaritiam imitantur, usuras committunt, pauperes gravant, opprimuntque subjectos, filios suos ac filias vendunt servituti peccati, et subdunt jugo diaboli, non reprimendo eos a vitiis, sed magis inducendo ad vanitates. Docentur quoque majores prælati exemplo Nehemiæ, peccantes quamvis potentes et magnos, sine personarum acceptione strenue increpare, salubriter exhortari, atque ad condignam suorum exsecutionem officiorum seriosissime admonere. Imo omnes qui præsunt, docentur hic suis subditis in temporalibus et spiritualibus, præsertim inopiæ tempore liberaliter subvenire, non otio, loquacitati, voluptative gustus et tactus vacare; sed in omni opere virtuoso se ipsos in primis exemplares et alacres exhibere, et contentari sobrio cibo, modico potu, mediocrique somno.
paras.en: From this chapter we are taught works of mercy; but alas! now many most unhappy men, Christians in name only, imitate the avarice of the Jews, commit usury, burden the poor and oppress their subjects, sell their sons and daughters into the bondage of sin and put them under the devil's yoke, not restraining them from vices but rather leading them on to vanities. Greater prelates too are taught by the example of Nehemias to rebuke sinners vigorously, however powerful and great, without respect of persons[[1 Tim 5:20||]], to exhort them for their salvation, and to admonish them most earnestly to the worthy carrying out of their offices. Nay, all who are set over others are taught here to help their subjects liberally in temporal and spiritual things, above all in a time of want; not to give themselves to idleness, talk, or the pleasure of taste and touch; but to show themselves first of all a pattern and eager in every virtuous work, and to be content with sober food, little drink, and moderate sleep.

6.title: Explanatio capituli sexti: Factum est autem quum audisset Sanaballat
6.title_en: Explanation of the sixth chapter: And it came to pass, when Sanaballat heard

paras.t: Describuntur hic insidiæ ipsi Nehemiæ illatæ.
paras.en: Here are described the plots laid against Nehemias himself.

paras.t: Factum est autem quum audisset Sanaballat et Tobias et Gossem, qui inter adversarios Nehemiæ erant principales, quod ædificassem murum, et non esset in ipso interruptio, quia jam erat integratus et continuatus; miserunt ad me, dicentes simulatorie: Veni, et percutiamus fœdus, id est, pactum pacis et amicitiæ ineamus firmissime: ideo additur, In vitulis, id est ipsum fœdus roborando per occisiones vitulorum, in signum quod morte dignus consisteret, qui pactum hoc violaret. Fuit namque antiquitus consuetudo, ut in confœderatione hujusmodi occideretur vitulus unus aut plures, aut alia pecora, in signum firmitatis, atque ad designandum quod mortem mereretur qui fœdus transgrederetur. Hinc per Jeremiam loquitur Dominus: Dabo viros qui prævaricantur fœdus meum, et non observaverunt verba fœderis, quibus assensi sunt in conspectu meo, vitulum quem conciderunt in duas partes, et transierunt inter divisiones illas. Ex quo elicitur, quod in signum firmitatis consueverunt etiam semel ire inter partes animalis occisi atque divisi. In campo uno. Volebant enim Nehemiam trahere extra urbem, quatenus in rure occiderent eum. Hinc subditur: Ipsi autem cogitabant ut facerent mihi malum. Deinde in littera ponitur excusatio Nehemiæ, et planus est textus.
paras.en: [[6:1|And it came to pass, when Sanaballat, and Tobias, and Gossem|Factum est autem quum audisset Sanaballat et Tobias et Gossem]], who were the chief among the adversaries of Nehemias, [[6:1|heard that I had built the wall|quod ædificassem murum]], [[6:1|and that there was no breach left in it|et non esset in ipso interruptio]], since it was now whole and continuous, they [[6:2|sent to me, saying|miserunt ad me, dicentes]] deceitfully: [[6:2|Come, and let us make a league together|Veni, et percutiamus fœdus]], that is, let us enter most firmly into a pact of peace and friendship: and so it is added, [[6:2|in the villages|In vitulis]] [Denis reads *in vitulis*, “with calves”, for *in viculis*, “in the villages”, which the margin gives], that is, strengthening the league itself by the slaying of calves, in sign that whoever broke this pact would be worthy of death. For it was the custom of old that in a league of this kind one calf or more, or other beasts, were slain in sign of its firmness, and to signify that whoever transgressed the league would deserve death. Hence the Lord speaks by Jeremias: [[Jer 34:18|And I will give the men that have transgressed my covenant, and have not performed the words of the covenant which they agreed to in my presence, when they cut the calf in two and passed between the parts thereof|Dabo viros qui prævaricantur fœdus meum, et non observaverunt verba fœderis, quibus assensi sunt in conspectu meo, vitulum quem conciderunt in duas partes, et transierunt inter divisiones illas]]. From which it is gathered that in sign of firmness they were also accustomed to pass once between the parts of the animal slain and divided. [[6:2|in the plain of Ono|In campo uno]] [Denis's text has *uno*, “one”; the margin gives *Ono*]. For they wished to draw Nehemias out of the city so as to kill him in the country. Hence it is added: [[6:2|But they thought to do me mischief|Ipsi autem cogitabant ut facerent mihi malum]]. Then the letter gives Nehemias's excuse, and the text is plain.

paras.t: Et immisit ad me Sanaballat, juxta verbum prius, id est insidiose, sicut et ante; non tamen verba præferentia speciem amicitiæ, sed comminationis. Aliquando tamen verba amicitiæ addidit simulatorie, sicut subjungitur: puerum, id est ministrum, et epistolam scriptam hoc modo: In gentibus auditum est, id est, inter nos gentiles jam publice vulgatum est, et Gossem, cui tanquam viro solenni credendum est, dixit, quod tu et Judæi cogitetis rebellare contra regem Persarum. Propter quam causam et prophetas posueris, qui prædicent de te in Jerusalem, id est, quosdam induxeris ad hoc, quod simulant se spiritum prophetiæ habere, dicentes quasi ex revelatione divina: Rex in Juda est, id est, ex Dei voluntate Nehemias iste est rex terræ et populi hujus: ideo ei, non regi Persarum, obediatis. Auditurus est rex hæc, id est, percipiet ista, et indignabitur tibi; idcirco veni, ut ineamus consilium pariter, qualiter possis te excusare. Et misi ad eos, dicens, specialiter ad Sanaballat, tanquam ad capitaneum iniquorum: Non est factum secundum verba hæc quæ loqueris per epistolam quam misisti. Quam ob causam magis confortavi manus meas, id est, tanto plus animavi me ad operandum, quanto multiplicius ac insidiosius impius ille volebat me impedire. Sic et nos debemus tanto ferventius Deo servire, vitiisque resistere, quanto importunius invisibiles adversarii nos impugnant, aut homines pravi impedire nostrum profectum nituntur.
paras.en: [[6:5|And Sanaballat sent|Et immisit ad me Sanaballat]] to me, [[6:5|according to the former word|juxta verbum prius]], that is, treacherously, as before; yet not with words that bore a show of friendship, but of threatening. Yet sometimes he added words of friendship deceitfully, as follows: [[6:5|his servant|puerum]], that is, his minister, [[6:5|and he had a letter in his hand written in this manner|et epistolam scriptam hoc modo]]: [[6:6|It is reported amongst the Gentiles|In gentibus auditum est]], that is, it is now publicly spread abroad among us gentiles, [[6:6|and Gossem hath said it|et Gossem dixit]], who as a man of weight is to be believed, [[6:6|that thou and the Jews think to rebel|quod tu et Judæi cogitetis rebellare]] against the king of the Persians. [[6:6|for which end|Propter quam causam]] [[6:7|Thou hast also set up prophets|et prophetas posueris]], [[6:7|to preach of thee at Jerusalem|qui prædicent de te in Jerusalem]], that is, thou hast induced certain men to pretend that they have the spirit of prophecy, [[6:7|saying|dicentes]] as if by divine revelation: [[6:7|There is a king in Judea|Rex in Juda est]], that is, by the will of God this Nehemias is king of this land and people: therefore obey him, not the king of the Persians. [[6:7|The king will hear of these things|Auditurus est rex hæc]], that is, he will learn of them, and will be angry with thee; [[6:7|therefore come now, that we may take counsel together|idcirco veni, ut ineamus consilium pariter]], how thou mayest excuse thyself. [[6:8|And I sent to them, saying|Et misi ad eos, dicens]], to Sanaballat especially, as to the captain of the wicked: [[6:8|There is no such thing done as thou sayest|Non est factum secundum verba hæc quæ loqueris]] in the letter thou hast sent. [[6:9|Wherefore I strengthened my hands the more|Quam ob causam magis confortavi manus meas]], that is, I spurred myself on to the work the more, the more manifoldly and treacherously that wicked man wished to hinder me. So we too ought to serve God and resist vices the more fervently, the more importunately our invisible adversaries assail us, or wicked men strive to hinder our progress.

paras.t: Et ingressus sum domum Semaiæ Judæi, quem mihi fidelem esse putavi, qui ait: Tractemus nobiscum in domo Dei, id est inter nos conferamus in templo, qualiter tu, Nehemia, evadere possis pericula, et claudamus portas ædis, id est domus Dei, ut intra templum maneas clausus; quia venturi sunt Sanaballat et sui, ut interficiant te. Et dixi, refutando talem suggestionem: Num quisquam similis mei fugit? id est, numquid aliquis in Deo confidens, et quæ Dei sunt agens, fugere habet timore humano? Et quis ut ego, id est, quis similis mei in Dei confidentia, ingredietur templum fugiendo hostes, et vivet? ac si dicat: Si sic fugeret timore inordinato, mereretur divino privari auxilio, et occidi. Nihilominus licitum est ex rationabili causa, et ex naturali mortis timore, præsidium fugæ assumere, et locum sacrum ac tutum intrare, sicut et David sanctus frequenter fugit a facie Saul. Non tamen id licitum est in derogationem justitiæ, atque in detrimentum boni communis, sicut in proposito isto. Ad hoc enim falsarius iste voluit Nehemiam in templo recludere, ut opus Dei negligeretur, et Nehemias notaretur de fuga formidolosa, quasi non sperans in Domino.
paras.en: [[6:10|And I went into the house of Samaia|Et ingressus sum domum Semaiæ]] the Jew, whom I thought faithful to me, who said: [[6:10|Let us consult together in the house of God|Tractemus nobiscum in domo Dei]], that is, let us confer together in the temple how thou, Nehemias, mayest escape the dangers, [[6:10|and let us shut the doors of the temple|et claudamus portas ædis]], that is, of the house of God, so that thou mayest stay shut up within the temple; [[6:10|for they will come to kill thee|quia venturi sunt ut interficiant te]], Sanaballat and his men. [[6:11|And I said|Et dixi]], refuting such a suggestion: [[6:11|Should such a man as I flee?|Num quisquam similis mei fugit?]] that is, should anyone who trusts in God and does the things of God flee out of human fear? [[6:11|and who is there that being as I am|Et quis ut ego]], that is, who that is like me in trust in God, [[6:11|would go into the temple, to save his life?|ingredietur templum fugiendo hostes, et vivet?]] fleeing from the enemy; as if to say: if he fled so out of inordinate fear, he would deserve to be deprived of divine help and to be slain. Nevertheless it is lawful, for a reasonable cause and from the natural fear of death, to take the protection of flight and to enter a holy and safe place, as holy David too often fled from the face of Saul. But it is not lawful to the prejudice of justice and to the detriment of the common good, as in the case before us. For this forger wished to shut Nehemias up in the temple so that the work of God would be neglected, and Nehemias would be branded with a fearful flight, as though he did not hope in the Lord.

paras.t: Et intellexi, ex divino instinctu seu consideratione industriæ meæ, quod Deus non misisset eum, id est, ex divina directione mihi talia non proferret. Sicque de spirituali, non locali, missione intelligitur istud, quemadmodum tertio Regum Ahias senex et cæcus dixit ad uxorem Jeroboam ad se missam: Ego missus sum ad te durus nuntius. Sed quasi vaticinans, id est non vere, sed apparenter prophetans, locutus esset ad me. Magis enim debuerat consulere Nehemiæ, ut confidendo in Domino, præpararet se ad resistendum adversariis illis divini cultus ac boni communis, quam ut ita recluderet se. Acceperat enim pretium, id est pecuniam a Sanaballat, ut ita deciperet me, et haberent malum, id est, aliquam culpam scirent de me, quod exprobrarent, id est, insultarent atque objicerent, mihi. Memento mei, Domine, pro Tobia et Sanaballat, id est, a talibus erue me, juxta opera eorum talia, ut eis pœnam justam infligas, propter tam vitiosa verba eorum et gesta. Mihi autem miserearis, eo quod tanta ac talia ab ipsis injuste perpessus sim. Sed et Noadiæ prophetæ et ceterorum prophetarum qui terrebant me, id est, illorum pseudoprophetarum volentium me perterrere, memento per debitam eorum castigationem saltem in vita hac, ne pereant in æternum.
paras.en: [[6:12|And I understood that God had not sent him|Et intellexi quod Deus non misisset eum]], by a divine prompting or by my own careful consideration: that is, that he was not putting such things to me by divine direction. And so this is understood of a spiritual, not a local, sending, as in the third book of Kings Ahias, old and blind, said to the wife of Jeroboam, who had been sent to him: [[3 Kings 14:6|I am sent to thee with heavy tidings|Ego missus sum ad te durus nuntius]]. [[6:12|but that he had spoken to me as if he had been prophesying|sed quasi vaticinans locutus esset ad me]], that is, not truly but in appearance prophesying. For he ought rather to have counselled Nehemias, trusting in the Lord, to prepare himself to resist those adversaries of the divine worship and of the common good, than so to shut himself up. [[6:13|For he had taken money|Acceperat enim pretium]], that is, money from Sanaballat, to deceive me so, [[6:13|and they might have some evil|et haberent malum]], that is, might know of some fault in me, [[6:13|to upbraid me withal|quod exprobrarent mihi]], that is, to insult me with and cast up at me. [[6:14|Remember me, O Lord, for Tobias and Sanaballat|Memento mei, Domine, pro Tobia et Sanaballat]], that is, deliver me from such men, [[6:14|according to their works of this kind|juxta opera eorum talia]], so that thou mayest inflict just punishment on them for their so vicious words and deeds; but have mercy on me, because I have unjustly suffered so many and such things from them. [[6:14|and Noadias the prophet, and the rest of the prophets that would have put me in fear|Sed et Noadiæ prophetæ et ceterorum prophetarum qui terrebant me]], that is, of those false prophets who wished to terrify me, remember them by their due chastisement, at least in this life, lest they perish for ever.

paras.t: Completus est autem murus Jerusalem vicesimo quinto die mensis Elul: qui dicitur esse sextus mensis apud Judæos, ac correspondere communiter partim nostro Augusto, et partim Septembri; quinquaginta duobus diebus. Quo constat, quam ferventer ac fortiter laboraverunt. Unde de tam expedita et celeri consummatione muri, consternati sunt adversarii, videntes hoc fieri non potuisse absque speciali Omnipotentis subsidio. Et hoc est quod subditur: Factum est autem quum audissent, etc.
paras.en: [[6:15|But the wall was finished the five and twentieth day of the month of Elul|Completus est autem murus Jerusalem vicesimo quinto die mensis Elul]], which is said to be the sixth month among the Jews, and to correspond commonly partly to our August and partly to September; [[6:15|in two and fifty days|quinquaginta duobus diebus]]. From which it is clear how fervently and strongly they laboured. Hence at so speedy and swift a completion of the wall the adversaries were dismayed, seeing that it could not have been done without the special help of the Almighty. And this is what is added: [[6:16|And it came to pass when all our enemies heard of it|Factum est autem quum audissent]], etc.

paras.t: Sed et in diebus illis multæ optimatum Judæorum epistolæ mittebantur ad Tobiam, id est, multi majores inter Judæos miserunt frequenter epistolas ad Tobiam, Samaritanum habitatione, sed Ammoniten natione, ut patet supra; et a Tobia veniebant ad eos epistolæ. Multi enim erant in Juda habentes juramentum ejus, id est, confœderati ei cum jurejurando, quia gener erat, id est, filiam habuit Secheniæ in uxorem: qui Sechenias fuit unus de præcipuis inter Judæos; et Johanan filius ejus, puta Tobiæ, acceperat filiam Mosollam inter Judæos notabilis viri. Sicque per conjugia fuit inter istos Judæos et Samaritanos amicitia et confœderatio facta: quod periculosum fuit Nehemiæ, quum non sit nequior pestis, quam hostis familiaris, cui dum creditur, periculum improvise incurritur. Tamen quod dictum est, Johanan filius ejus, ad Secheniam posset referri. Sed et laudabant eum, puta Tobiam, coram me, ut inirem pactum cum illo. Et verba mea nuntiabant ei secrete per scripta seu nuntios.
paras.en: [[6:17|Moreover in those days many letters were sent by the principal men of the Jews to Tobias|Sed et in diebus illis multæ optimatum Judæorum epistolæ mittebantur ad Tobiam]], that is, many of the greater men among the Jews often sent letters to Tobias, a Samaritan by dwelling but an Ammonite by nation, as is plain above[[2 Esd 4:3||]]; [[6:17|and from Tobias there came letters to them|et a Tobia veniebant ad eos epistolæ]]. [[6:18|For there were many in Judea sworn to him|Multi enim erant in Juda habentes juramentum ejus]], that is, leagued with him by oath, [[6:18|because he was the son in law|quia gener erat]], that is, he had the daughter of Sechenias to wife, which Sechenias was one of the chief men among the Jews; [[6:18|and Johanan his son had taken to wife the daughter of Mosollam|et Johanan filius ejus, puta Tobiæ, acceperat filiam Mosollam]], namely Tobias's son, the daughter of a notable man among the Jews. And so through marriages friendship and alliance were made between these Jews and the Samaritans: which was dangerous for Nehemias, since there is no worse plague than an enemy of one's own household, for while he is trusted, danger is run into unawares. Yet what is said, *Johanan his son*, could be referred to Sechenias. [[6:19|And they praised him also before me|Sed et laudabant eum, puta Tobiam, coram me]], namely Tobias, so that I would make a pact with him. [[6:19|and they related my words to him|Et verba mea nuntiabant ei]] secretly by writings or messengers.

paras.t: Unde constat, quam verissime scriptum sit, Multæ tribulationes justorum: quia Nehemiam justum qui tam beneficus et liberalissimus fuit in suos, imo in totum populum Judæorum, tantaque bona exhibuit eis, et pro communi eorum bono tam infatigabiliter laboravit, ita sunt persecuti, non solum Samaritani et alieni, sed et populus ejus et notabiliores eorum. Patientiam ergo discamus, nec propter quamcumque persecutionem a via justitiæ recedamus, confidentes semper in Domino. Innotescit demum ex introductis, quod Judæi post reditum a Babylonica captivitate cito recesserunt a Domino pro magna parte: imo multa magna commiserunt peccata, ac profana contraxerunt contra legem connubia.
paras.en: Hence it is clear how very truly it is written: [[Ps 33:20|Many are the afflictions of the just|Multæ tribulationes justorum]]: for the just Nehemias, who was so beneficent and most liberal towards his own, nay towards the whole people of the Jews, and showed them so many good things, and laboured so tirelessly for their common good, was so persecuted not only by the Samaritans and strangers but by his own people and the more notable of them. Let us learn patience, then, and not depart from the way of justice for any persecution, trusting always in the Lord[[Jer 17:7||]]. Lastly, it becomes known from what has been brought in that the Jews, after their return from the Babylonian captivity, soon fell away from the Lord in great part: indeed they committed many great sins, and contracted unholy marriages against the law.

7.title: Expositio capituli septimi: Postquam autem ædificatus est murus
7.title_en: Exposition of the seventh chapter: Now after the wall was built

paras.t: Sententia hujus capituli quasi tota contenta est supra. Præmittitur tamen hic aliquid, quod ibi non legitur.
paras.en: The substance of this chapter is almost wholly contained above[[1 Esd 2:1||]]. Yet something is set first here which is not read there.

paras.t: Postquam autem ædificatus est murus Jerusalem, prout præcedenti habetur capitulo, et posui valvas, id est portas seu januas, in portarum structuris seu in templo, et recensui, id est numeravi, janitores et cantores templi, et Levitas; et dixi: Non aperiantur portæ Jerusalem usque ad calorem solis, id est, quousque sol notabiliter super nostrum horizontem ascendat, ita quod calor ex reflexione radiorum solarium causetur in terra. Quumque adhuc adsisterent mihi viri, quibus hæc dixi, portæ Jerusalem clausæ sunt ante solis occasum, et oppilatæ, id est obturatæ ad insultum hostium repellendum. Nam pauci adhuc in Jerusalem morabantur. Et posui custodes ad vigilandum per noctes, secundum vices suas et ex opposito domorum suarum in muro. Et non erant domus ædificatæ ad sufficientiam.
paras.en: [[7:1|Now after the wall was built|Postquam autem ædificatus est murus]] of Jerusalem, as we have it in the preceding chapter[[2 Esd 6:15||]], [[7:1|and I had set up the doors|et posui valvas]], that is, the gates or doors, in the structures of the gates or in the temple, [[7:1|and numbered the porters and singing men, and Levites|et recensui janitores, et cantores, et Levitas]] of the temple; [[7:3|And I said to them|et dixi]]: [[7:3|Let not the gates of Jerusalem be opened till the sun be hot|Non aperiantur portæ Jerusalem usque ad calorem solis]], that is, until the sun has risen well above our horizon, so that heat is caused on the earth by the reflection of the sun's rays. [[7:3|And while they were yet standing by|Quumque adhuc adsisterent]] me, the men to whom I said this, [[7:3|the gates were shut|portæ Jerusalem clausæ sunt]] before sunset, [[7:3|and barred|et oppilatæ]], that is, blocked up to repel an assault of the enemy. For few as yet dwelt in Jerusalem. [[7:3|and I set watchmen|Et posui custodes]] to keep watch by night, [[7:3|every one by their courses, and every man over against his house|secundum vices suas et ex opposito domorum suarum]] on the wall. [[7:4|and the houses were not built|Et non erant domus ædificatæ]] in sufficient number.

paras.t: Deus autem dedit in corde meo, id est, inspiravit mihi ut facerem quod subditur: et congregavi optimates et magistratus et vulgus, ut recenserem eos, id est numerarem, sicque disponerem de populatione urbis Jerusalem; et inveni librum census, id est numerationis, eorum qui ascenderant primum, id est, cum Zorobabel de Babylonia redierunt in prima licentia a Cyro data, et inventum est scriptum in eo, id est in libro illo: Isti filii provinciæ qui ascenderunt de captivitate, etc. Ista verba scripta sunt ab Esdra, ibique exposita, eademque summa totius multitudinis hic et ibi exprimitur; sed quædam nomina variantur, quoniam multi eorum duo aut plura nomina habuerunt.
paras.en: [[7:5|But God had put in my heart|Deus autem dedit in corde meo]], that is, inspired me to do what follows: [[7:5|and I assembled the princes and magistrates, and common people|et congregavi optimates et magistratus et vulgus]], [[7:5|to number them|ut recenserem eos]], that is, to count them, and so to make arrangements for peopling the city of Jerusalem; [[7:5|and I found a book of the number of them who came up at first|et inveni librum census, id est numerationis, eorum qui ascenderant primum]], that is, who returned from Babylonia with Zorobabel under the first leave given by Cyrus, [[7:5|and therein it was found written|et inventum est scriptum in eo]], that is, in that book: [[7:6|These are the children of the province, who came up from the captivity|Isti filii provinciæ qui ascenderunt de captivitate]], etc. These words were written by Esdras[[1 Esd 2:1||]] and expounded there, and the same total of the whole multitude is given here and there; but some names vary, since many of them had two or more names.

paras.t: Nonnulli autem de principibus familiarum dederunt in opus. Hoc est quod supra scriptum est: Et de principibus patrum, quum ingrederentur templum Domini quod est in Jerusalem, sponte obtulerunt in domum Dei ad exstruendam eam in impensas operis auri solidos sexaginta millia, etc. Verumtamen quæ ibi dicuntur quasi in generali, hic specialius exprimuntur: et ita quantum ad particulares descriptiones, differentia invenitur inter verba hujus passus atque illius.
paras.en: [[7:70|And some of the heads of the families gave unto the work|Nonnulli autem de principibus familiarum dederunt in opus]]. This is what was written above: [[1 Esd 2:68|And some of the chief of the fathers, when they came to the temple of the Lord, which is in Jerusalem, offered freely to the house of the Lord to build it|Et de principibus patrum, quum ingrederentur templum Domini quod est in Jerusalem, sponte obtulerunt in domum Dei ad exstruendam eam]], [[1 Esd 2:69|they gave towards the expenses of the work|in impensas operis]] sixty thousand solids of gold, etc. Yet what is said there as it were in general is set out here more particularly: and so, as regards the particular descriptions, a difference is found between the words of this passage and of that.

8.title: Explanatio capituli octavi: Et venerat mensis septimus
8.title_en: Explanation of the eighth chapter: And the seventh month came

paras.t: Post templi ac civitatis Jerusalem reædificationem, recitatur hic cultus Dei secundum legem in locis eisdem.
paras.en: After the rebuilding of the temple and of the city of Jerusalem, the worship of God according to the law in those same places is related here.

paras.t: Et venerat mensis septimus secundum Hebræorum computationem: et agitur hic de anno consummationis murorum Jerusalem. Porro quod subditur in multis codicibus, Scenopegiæ sub Esdra et Nehemia, non est de textu. Congregatusque est omnis populus, præsertim in Jerusalem habitans, aliarumque urbium principales habitatores, quasi vir unus, id est concorditer et perfecte, in platea, quæ est ante portam Aquarum: quæ supra dicta est porta Fontis. In cujus opposito fuit atrium templi, in quo populus confluxit ad orandum, audiendumque verbum Dei: quod quidam dicunt hic designari per plateam. Et dixerunt Esdræ scribæ, ut afferret librum legis.
paras.en: [[8:1|And the seventh month came|Et venerat mensis septimus]] according to the reckoning of the Hebrews: and the year in question is that of the completion of the walls of Jerusalem. What is added in many copies, *of the Scenopegia* [the feast of Tabernacles] *under Esdras and Nehemias*, is not of the text. [[8:1|And all the people were gathered together as one man|Congregatusque est omnis populus quasi vir unus]], especially those living in Jerusalem, and the chief inhabitants of the other cities, that is, with one accord and perfectly, [[8:1|to the street which is before the water gate|in platea, quæ est ante portam Aquarum]], which above was called the gate of the Fountain[[2 Esd 3:15||]]. Opposite it was the court of the temple, into which the people flocked to pray and to hear the word of God: which some say is signified here by the street. [[8:1|and they spoke to Esdras the scribe, to bring the book of the law|Et dixerunt Esdræ scribæ, ut afferret librum legis]].

paras.t: Attulit ergo Esdras legem coram multitudine in die […]. Et legit Esdras in eo aperte, id est intelligibiliter et distincte: quia sic legi debet, præsertim divina Scriptura; de mane usque ad medium diem: in quo patet fervor suæ devotionis; die prima mensis septimi: in quo die fuit festum Tubarum in memoriam liberationis Isaac ab immolatione in holocaustum, quando pro eo oblatus est aries, qui inter vepres cornibus hæsit, prout in Genesi scribitur. Hinc in Levitico loquitur Dominus: Mense septimo prima die mensis erit festum Tubarum. Et aures omnis populi erant erectæ ad librum: quia cum diligentia et aviditate audiendum est verbum Dei juxta illud Jacobi, Sit omnis homo velox ad audiendum. Hinc scriptum est in Ecclesiastico: Auris bona cum omni concupiscentia audiet sapientiam. In hoc quoque patuit audientium fervor, quod per tot horas non lassabantur verba salubria audiendo. Et benedixit Esdras Domino Deo voce magna, ipsum laudando. Et legerunt in libro legis distincte et aperte; et intellexerunt quum legeretur, specialiter Esdras, deinde et Nehemias ac quidam Levitæ. Unde subjungitur:
paras.en: [[8:2|Then Esdras the priest brought the law before the multitude|Attulit ergo Esdras legem coram multitudine]] on the day […] [the OCR breaks off here]. [[8:3|And he read it plainly|Et legit Esdras in eo aperte]], that is, intelligibly and distinctly: for so it ought to be read, above all the divine Scripture; [[8:3|from the morning until midday|de mane usque ad medium diem]]: in which the fervour of his devotion is plain; [[8:2|in the first day of the seventh month|die prima mensis septimi]]: on which day was the feast of Trumpets, in memory of the deliverance of Isaac from being sacrificed as a holocaust, when in his place the ram was offered that was caught by its horns among the briers, as is written in Genesis[[Gen 22:13||]]. Hence in Leviticus the Lord says: [[Lev 23:24|The seventh month, on the first day of the month|Mense septimo prima die mensis]] there shall be the feast of Trumpets. [[8:3|and the ears of all the people were attentive to the book|Et aures omnis populi erant erectæ ad librum]]: for the word of God is to be heard with care and eagerness, according to that saying of James, [[Jas 1:19|let every man be swift to hear|Sit omnis homo velox ad audiendum]]. Hence it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 3:31|a good ear will hear wisdom with all desire|Auris bona cum omni concupiscentia audiet sapientiam]]. In this too the fervour of the hearers was plain, that through so many hours they did not tire of hearing the wholesome words. [[8:6|And Esdras blessed the Lord the great God|Et benedixit Esdras Domino Deo voce magna]] [Denis reads *voce magna*, “with a loud voice”, for *magno*, “the great”], praising Him. [[8:8|And they read in the book of the law of God distinctly and plainly|Et legerunt in libro legis distincte et aperte]]; [[8:8|and they understood when it was read|et intellexerunt quum legeretur]], Esdras especially, and then Nehemias and certain Levites. Hence it is added:

paras.t: Dixit autem Nehemias (ipse est Athersatha) et Esdras et Levitæ interpretantes universo populo, id est exponentes turbæ vulgarium quæ legebantur, vel successive vel unus uni parti, alter alteri, secundum quod in Actis habetur: Nonne isti omnes qui loquuntur, Galilæi sunt? Dies sanctificatus est Domino Deo nostro, id est, dies iste ad Dei honorem solennis est. Nolite lugere. Flebat enim omnis populus, quum audiret verba legis, ex compunctione et contritione, quoniam verba legis audiendo consideraverunt suas transgressiones. Nec malum fuit quod flebant, sed bonum. Melius tamen pro die illo, ut gauderent in Domino ex contemplatione bonitatis et pietatis ipsius, beneficiorumque ejus. Actus enim virtutum sunt exercendi loco et tempore opportuno. Et dixit eis Nehemias: Ite, comedite pinguia, et bibite mulsum, id est potionem ex aqua et melle confectam; vel, ut quidam exponunt, vinum melle dulcoratum; et mittite partes his qui non præparaverunt sibi, præsertim egenis. Sic autem fuerant admonendi, quia a mane usque meridiem audierant verbum Dei, et quia solennitas erat jucunda. Gaudium enim Domini est fortitudo vestra, id est, Deus per modum gaudentis se habet de vestra spirituali confortatione in omni actu virtutum, quoniam amat vos et vestram cupit salutem. Qui in Jeremia testatur: Lætabor super eis quum benefecero eis. Etenim beneplacitum est Domino in populo suo. Qui per Salomonem fatetur: Deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum.
paras.en: [[8:9|And Nehemiah (he is Athersatha) and Esdras|Dixit autem Nehemias (ipse est Athersatha) et Esdras]] [[8:9|and the Levites who interpreted to all the people|et Levitæ interpretantes universo populo]] [the words of this lemma are garbled in the OCR and are read with the Vulgate], that is, expounding to the crowd of common people what was read, either one after another, or one to one part and another to another, as we have it in the Acts: [[Acts 2:7|are not all these that speak Galilean?|Nonne isti omnes qui loquuntur, Galilæi sunt?]] [[8:9|said: This is a holy day to the Lord our God|Dies sanctificatus est Domino Deo nostro]], that is, this day is solemn to the honour of God. [[8:9|do not mourn|Nolite lugere]]. [[8:9|for all the people wept, when they heard the words of the law|Flebat enim omnis populus, quum audiret verba legis]], from compunction and contrition, since in hearing the words of the law they considered their transgressions. Nor was it bad that they wept, but good. Yet it was better for that day that they should rejoice in the Lord in contemplating His goodness and kindness and His benefits. For acts of virtue are to be exercised in their fitting place and time. [[8:10|And he said to them|Et dixit eis Nehemias]]: [[8:10|Go, eat fat meats, and drink sweet wine|Ite, comedite pinguia, et bibite mulsum]] [*mulsum*], that is, a drink made of water and honey; or, as some explain, wine sweetened with honey; [[8:10|and send portions to them that have not prepared for themselves|et mittite partes his qui non præparaverunt sibi]], especially to the needy. They had to be admonished so because they had heard the word of God from morning till noon, and because the solemnity was a joyful one. [[8:10|for the joy of the Lord is our strength|Gaudium enim Domini est fortitudo vestra]] [Denis reads *vestra*, “your”]: that is, God behaves as one who rejoices in your spiritual strengthening in every act of virtue, since He loves you and desires your salvation. He testifies in Jeremias: [[Jer 32:41|I will rejoice over them, when I shall do them good|Lætabor super eis quum benefecero eis]]. For [[Ps 149:4|the Lord is well pleased with his people|beneplacitum est Domino in populo suo]]. He declares by Solomon: [[Prov 8:31|my delights were to be with the children of men|Deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum]].

paras.t: Et invenerunt scriptum in lege, præcepisse Dominum in manu Moysi, id est per vocem et obsequium Moysi, ut habitarent filii Israel in tabernaculis factis de arborum ramis, in die solenni, id est in solennium dierum congerie, utpote septem diebus, mense septimo. Scriptum est enim in Levitico: A quintodecimo die mensis hujus septimi, erunt feriæ Tabernaculorum septem diebus. Quod jussum fuit in memoriam beneficii Dei, quo post eductionem filiorum Israel ex Ægypto, fecit eos habitare in tabernaculis et papilionibus atque tentoriis in deserto. Idcirco in Levitico Dominus ait: Ut discant posteri vestri, quod in tabernaculis habitare fecerim Israel, quum educerem eos de terra Ægypti. Et ut prædicent et divulgent vocem in universis urbibus suis. Nam ex præfato præcepto sacerdotes et scribæ erant adstricti populum Israel de hujus festi observantia informare. Egredimini in montem, et afferte frondes olivæ, et frondes ligni pulcherrimi, frondes myrti, et ramos palmarum, ut fiant tabernacula, sicut scriptum est.
paras.en: [[8:14|And they found written in the law|Et invenerunt scriptum in lege]], [[8:14|that the Lord had commanded by the hand of Moses|præcepisse Dominum in manu Moysi]] [these words are garbled in the OCR and are read with the Vulgate], that is, by the voice and service of Moses, [[8:14|that the children of Israel should dwell in tabernacles|ut habitarent filii Israel in tabernaculis]] made of the branches of trees, [[8:14|on the feast|in die solenni]], that is, in a run of solemn days, namely seven days, [[8:14|in the seventh month|mense septimo]]. For it is written in Leviticus: [[Lev 23:34|From the fifteenth day of this same seventh month, shall be kept the feast of tabernacles, seven days|A quintodecimo die mensis hujus septimi, erunt feriæ Tabernaculorum septem diebus]]. This was commanded in memory of the benefit of God by which, after bringing the children of Israel out of Egypt, He made them dwell in tabernacles, pavilions and tents in the desert. Therefore in Leviticus the Lord says: [[Lev 23:43|That your posterity may know, that I made the children of Israel to dwell in tabernacles, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt|Ut discant posteri vestri, quod in tabernaculis habitare fecerim Israel, quum educerem eos de terra Ægypti]]. [[8:15|And that they should proclaim and publish the word in all their cities|Et ut prædicent et divulgent vocem in universis urbibus suis]]. For by the aforesaid command the priests and scribes were bound to instruct the people of Israel about the keeping of this feast. [[8:15|Go forth to the mount, and fetch branches of olive, and branches of beautiful wood, branches of myrtle, and branches of palm|Egredimini in montem, et afferte frondes olivæ, et frondes ligni pulcherrimi, frondes myrti, et ramos palmarum]], [[8:15|to make tabernacles, as it is written|ut fiant tabernacula, sicut scriptum est]].

paras.t: Et egressus est omnis populus, et attulerunt, id est, quidam de omnibus ad afferendum ramos arborum: non itaque secundo die quo audierunt istud festum esse agendum, de quo die secundo, paulo ante habetur in littera; sed appropinquante et jam imminente quintodecimo die septimi mensis, quo die fuit hoc festum incipiendum. Feceruntque tabernacula unusquisque in domate suo, id est in tecto plano suæ domus: quia in terra illa, tecta domorum sunt plana, et tabernacula ista sub dio fiebant; et in atriis suis. Non enim fecerant a diebus Josue taliter filii Israel, id est tam solenniter festum hoc Tabernaculorum: quemadmodum quarto Regum libro legitur, quod a diebus Judicum non factum fuit tale Phase, quale fecit Josias rex. Aliqui tamen dicunt, quod comparatio ista sit intelligenda secundum quid, non simpliciter. Sed securius reor veritatem historiæ sequi et textum. Istud enim festum poterat celeberrime fieri absque notabili sumptu: et sub Esdra celebratum est cum devotione præcipua et grandi lætitia, atque a populo toto, et cum formosis variisque materiis: quia ut fertur in littera, attulerunt frondes olivæ ac ligni pulcherrimi, frondes myrti, id est arboris sic vocatæ, ramos palmarum, frondesque ligni nemorosi: in quibus omnibus sumitur singulare pro plurali.
paras.en: [[8:16|And the people went forth, and brought|Et egressus est omnis populus, et attulerunt]], that is, some out of all of them, to bring branches of trees: not on the second day, then, on which they heard that this feast was to be kept, of which second day the letter speaks a little before[[8:13||]]; but when the fifteenth day of the seventh month, on which this feast was to begin, was drawing near and was now at hand. [[8:16|And they made themselves tabernacles every man on the top of his house|Feceruntque tabernacula unusquisque in domate suo]], that is, on the flat roof of his house: for in that land the roofs of houses are flat, and these tabernacles were made under the open sky; [[8:16|and in their courts|et in atriis suis]]. [[8:17|for since the days of Josue the son of Nun the children of Israel had not done so|Non enim fecerant a diebus Josue taliter filii Israel]], that is, had not kept this feast of Tabernacles so solemnly: as we read in the fourth book of Kings that from the days of the Judges no such Phase had been kept as king Josias kept[[4 Kings 23:22||]]. Some say, however, that this comparison is to be understood in a certain respect, not simply. But I think it safer to follow the truth of the history and the text. For this feast could be kept most splendidly without notable expense; and under Esdras it was celebrated with singular devotion and great joy, and by the whole people, and with fine and varied materials: for, as the letter has it, they brought [[8:15|branches of olive, and branches of beautiful wood, branches of myrtle, and branches of palm, and branches of thick trees|frondes olivæ ac ligni pulcherrimi, frondes myrti, id est arboris sic vocatæ, ramos palmarum, frondesque ligni nemorosi]] [Denis has *frondes olivæ ac ligni pulcherrimi, frondes myrti, id est arboris sic vocatæ, ramos palmarum, frondesque ligni nemorosi*, glossing myrtle as “the tree so called”]: in all of which the singular is taken for the plural.

paras.t: Legit autem Esdras in libro legis per dies singulos mensis istius, seu festorum ipsius, a die primo hujus septimi mensis, usque ad diem novissimum mensis ejusdem; et fecerunt solennitatem Tabernaculorum septem diebus, et in die octavo, scilicet proxime subsequente ultimum diem solennitatis præfatæ, collectam juxta ritum, id est quamdam pecuniarum collectionem pro emendis requisitis in cultu templi, secundum jussionem et observantiam legis. Fuitque dies illa octava multum solennis. Sicque et in ea videtur Esdras legisse in libro legis. Hinc in Levitico Dominus ait: Dies quoque octavus erit celeberrimus atque sanctissimus: est enim cœtus atque collectæ. Et, ut legitur, dabant tertiam partem sicli per annum ad emendum oleum, et ad panes propositionis, ad ligna, et ad sacrificia sempiterna.
paras.en: [[8:18|And he read in the book of the law of God day by day|Legit autem Esdras in libro legis per dies singulos]] of this month, or of its feasts, [[8:18|from the first day till the last|a die primo usque ad diem novissimum]] of the same month; [[8:18|and they kept the solemnity seven days|et fecerunt solennitatem Tabernaculorum septem diebus]], [[8:18|and in the eighth day a solemn assembly according to the manner|et in die octavo collectam juxta ritum]] [*collecta*, “assembly”, which Denis takes as a collection], namely on the day next after the last day of the aforesaid solemnity: that is, a collection of money for buying what was needed in the worship of the temple, according to the command and observance of the law. And that eighth day was very solemn; and so it seems that on it too Esdras read in the book of the law. Hence in Leviticus the Lord says: [[Lev 23:36|The eighth day also shall be most solemn and most holy|Dies quoque octavus erit celeberrimus atque sanctissimus]]: [[Lev 23:36|For it is the day of assembly and congregation|est enim cœtus atque collectæ]]. And, as we read, they gave the third part of a sicle a year[[2 Esd 10:32||]] to buy oil, and for the loaves of proposition, for wood, and for the perpetual sacrifices.

paras.t: At vero de spirituali significatione festi Tabernaculorum et Collectæ, dictum est super Leviticum. Debemus equidem septem diebus, id est omni tempore incolatus vitæ præsentis in tabernaculis habitare, tanquam peregrini et hospites in deserto sæculi hujus, et virtutum virore ornari ac adspirare ad patriam, quatenus die octavo, id est octava Resurrectionis seu mox post curriculum dierum hujus exsilii, colligamur in regno cælesti: de qua spirituali celebratione festi Tabernaculorum a Zacharia fit mysticus sermo. Insuper, ex isto capitulo instruuntur fideles diebus festivis vacare divinis et sacris sermonibus, ad ecclesiam convenire, et cum ingenti affectu verbum Dei audire: quod et singulis diebus festivis proponendum est eis intelligibiliter, distincte, aperte, plenarie. Et quamvis post hæc liceat paululum lautius refici, vitanda est tamen omnis carnalitas, superfluitas, et voluptas. Et de his quæ sobriæ supersunt refectioni, facienda est pauperibus eleemosyna liberalis, caritativa, et humilis.
paras.en: But of the spiritual meaning of the feast of Tabernacles and of the Assembly we have spoken on Leviticus. We ought indeed for seven days, that is, through the whole time of our sojourn in this present life, to dwell in tabernacles, as pilgrims and strangers in the desert of this world, and to be adorned with the greenness of the virtues and to aspire to our fatherland, so that on the eighth day, that is, the octave of the Resurrection, or straight after the course of the days of this exile, we may be gathered into the heavenly kingdom: of which spiritual keeping of the feast of Tabernacles Zacharias speaks in a mystical discourse[[Zach 14:16||]]. Moreover, the faithful are taught by this chapter on feast days to give themselves to divine and sacred discourses, to come together to church, and to hear the word of God with great affection: which on every feast day is to be set before them intelligibly, distinctly, plainly and fully. And though after this it is lawful to dine a little more generously, yet all carnality, excess and pleasure is to be avoided. And from what is left over from a sober meal, a liberal, charitable and humble alms is to be given to the poor.

9.title: Expositio capituli noni: In die autem vicesimo quarto
9.title_en: Exposition of the ninth chapter: And in the four and twentieth day

paras.t: Devotio populi sua peccata humiliter confitentis, Deumque laudantis, et ejus beneficia grata mente recolentis, hoc loco describitur.
paras.en: The devotion of the people is described in this place: humbly confessing their sins, praising God, and recalling His benefits with a grateful mind.

paras.t: In die autem vicesimo quarto mensis hujus septimi, convenerunt filii Israel in jejunio, et in saccis, et humus super eos. Audiendo namque quotidie legem, adverterunt enormitatem et multitudinem suorum excessuum. Festivitas autem Tabernaculorum septem durans diebus, et quintodecimo die septimi mensis inchoans, duravit usque ad diem vicesimum secundum mensis ejusdem exclusive; die autem vicesimo secundo fecerunt collectam, et die vicesimo tertio separaverunt alienigenas a sua communione: sicque statuerunt die sequente per jejunia et confessionem ac alia humilitatis compunctionisque signa et gesta, veniam deprecari, ac gratiam emendationis in posterum implorare.
paras.en: [[9:1|And in the four and twentieth day of the month|In die autem vicesimo quarto mensis hujus]], the seventh, [[9:1|the children of Israel came together|convenerunt filii Israel]] [[9:1|with fasting and with sackcloth, and earth upon them|in jejunio, et in saccis, et humus super eos]]. For by hearing the law daily they had noticed the enormity and the multitude of their transgressions. Now the feast of Tabernacles, which lasts seven days and begins on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, had run until the twenty-second day of that month, not including it; on the twenty-second day they held the solemn assembly [that is, the closing gathering of the feast], and on the twenty-third they separated the foreigners from their communion; and so they resolved, on the following day, to beg pardon by fasts and confession and other signs and acts of humility and compunction, and to implore the grace of amendment for the time to come.

paras.t: Convenerunt ergo in jejunio, id est concorditer jejunantes, et in saccis, id est vestibus asperis pœnitentialibus aut cilicinis induti, et humus, id est adspersio pulverum, super capita fuit eorum.
paras.en: They [[9:1|came together|Convenerunt]] therefore [[9:1|with fasting|in jejunio]], that is, fasting with one accord, [[9:1|and with sackcloth|et in saccis]], that is, clothed in rough penitential garments or garments of haircloth, [[9:1|and earth|et humus]], that is, a sprinkling of dust, was upon their heads.

paras.t: Et separatum est semen filiorum Israel ab omni filio alienigena. Hoc quidam exponunt de separatione conjugiorum initorum inter Judæos et gentes: de qua separatione dictum est primo Esdræ libro. Alii autem exponunt de separatione eorum ab Ammonitis et Moabitis, quia in lege audierant: Ammonites et Moabites non intrabunt in ecclesiam Dei. Additur etiam in Scholastica historia, quod statuerunt et ipsa jumenta debere jejunare; et pueros, usque ad pueros septem annorum.
paras.en: [[9:2|And the seed of the children of Israel separated themselves from every stranger|Et separatum est semen filiorum Israel ab omni filio alienigena]]. Some explain this of the separation of the marriages contracted between Jews and gentiles, a separation spoken of in the first book of Esdras[[1 Esd 10:1||]]. Others explain it of their separation from the Ammonites and Moabites, since they had heard in the law: [[Deut 23:3|The Ammonite and the Moabite|Ammonites et Moabites]] [[Deut 23:3|shall not enter into the church of the Lord|non intrabunt in ecclesiam Dei]]. It is added also in the Scholastic History that they decreed that even the beasts of burden should fast, and the children too, down to children of seven years.

paras.t: Et steterunt, et confitebantur peccata sua et iniquitates patrum suorum, quas fuerunt magna ex parte imitati: sicque et pro patribus suis defunctis orabant. Confitebantur autem peccata sua non sacramentali confessione, sicut fit in evangelica lege, sed coram Deo seu publice coram sacerdote, prout moris fuit in lege, juxta illud Psalmi: Dixi, Confitebor adversum me injustitiam meam Domino. Unde et Salomon dixit: Qui abscondit scelera sua, non dirigetur; qui autem confessus fuerit, et reliquerit ea, misericordiam consequetur.
paras.en: [[9:2|and they stood|Et steterunt]], [[9:2|and confessed their sins, and the iniquities of their fathers|et confitebantur peccata sua et iniquitates patrum suorum]], which they had in great part imitated; and so they prayed also for their dead fathers. They confessed their sins, however, not by sacramental confession, as is done under the law of the Gospel, but before God, or publicly before the priest, as was the custom under the law, according to that of the Psalm: [[Ps 31:5|I said I will confess against my self my injustice to the Lord|Dixi, Confitebor adversum me injustitiam meam Domino]]. Hence Solomon too said: [[Prov 28:13|He that hideth his sins, shall not prosper: but he that shall confess, and forsake them, shall obtain mercy|Qui abscondit scelera sua, non dirigetur; qui autem confessus fuerit, et reliquerit ea, misericordiam consequetur]].

paras.t: Et consurrexerunt ad standum, ut lectionem legis audirent; et legerunt in volumine legis Levitæ seu scribæ, quater in die, et quater in nocte confitebantur. In quo patet fervor devotionis eorum, et vigilantia magna in nocte. Et adorabant Dominum.
paras.en: [[9:3|And they rose up to stand|Et consurrexerunt ad standum]], to hear the reading of the law; [[9:3|and they read in the book of the law|et legerunt in volumine legis]] (the Levites, that is, or the scribes) [[9:3|four times in the day|quater in die]], [[9:3|and four times|et quater]] in the night [[9:3|they confessed|confitebantur]]. In this the fervour of their devotion is plain, and their great watchfulness in the night. [[9:3|and adored the Lord|Et adorabant Dominum]].

paras.t: De hoc Magister in historiis scribit: Convenerunt octies ad audiendum legem, quater in die, et quater in nocte. Lectione terminata, prostravit se populus ad orandum, et fiebant preces super eum a sacerdotibus, et tandem benedictio sacerdotalis. Ex quibus, secundum Bedam, Ecclesia traxit exemplum. Nam supra gradum fit lectio, prout paulo post leguntur Levitæ ascendisse super gradum, et Levitæ, id est diaconi, faciunt proclamationes in populo. Octies quoque infra diem et noctem ad ecclesiam convenitur, quamvis non penitus eodem modo quo tunc. Semel enim in nocte surgimus ad nocturnos, secundum illud, Media nocte surgebam ad confitendum tibi. In die vero septies psallimus, juxta illud, Septies in die laudem dixi tibi: videlicet in Laudibus, quæ consueverunt circa vel ante auroram cantari, et in Prima, Tertia, Sexta, Nona, Vesperis et Completorio. In singulis autem Horis pro lectione dicitur Capitulum. Postea prosternimur ad preces in diebus non festis, et subditur Oratio pro benedictione.
paras.en: Of this the Master [that is, Peter Comestor, the Master of the Histories] writes in the Histories: They came together eight times to hear the law, four times in the day and four times in the night. When the reading was over, the people prostrated themselves to pray, and prayers were said over them by the priests, and at the last the priestly blessing. From these things, according to Bede, the Church has taken her example. For the reading is done upon a step, as a little later the Levites are read to have gone up [[9:4|upon the step|super gradum]]; and the Levites, that is, the deacons, make the proclamations among the people. The faithful also come together to church eight times within the day and night, though not altogether in the same way as then. For once in the night we rise for the Nocturns, according to that: [[Ps 118:62|I rose at midnight to give praise to thee|Media nocte surgebam ad confitendum tibi]]. In the day we sing psalms seven times, according to that: [[Ps 118:164|Seven times a day I have given praise to thee|Septies in die laudem dixi tibi]]: namely at Lauds, which are customarily sung about or before dawn, and at Prime, Terce, Sext, None, Vespers and Compline. In each of the Hours the Chapter is said in place of a reading. Afterwards, on days that are not feasts, we prostrate ourselves for the prayers, and the Collect is added for the blessing.

paras.t: Surrexerunt autem supra gradum Levitæ, qui in littera exprimuntur, et dixerunt: Surgite et benedicite Domino viventi, ab æterno et usque in æternum: cui in præsenti temporaliter, et in futuro æternaliter benedicunt electi; et benedicant omnes rationales creaturæ nomini gloriæ tuæ, id est tibi ipsi glorioso, excelso, id est residenti in summo cœlo; vel, in sublimi devotione id agant. Unde et angeli nato Christo ex Virgine cecinerunt: Gloria in excelsis Deo. In omni benedictione, id est plena et perfecta commendatione tuæ bonitatis et perfectionis in semetipsa, et laude ejusdem propter opera et beneficia sua, seu per respectum et habitudinem ad creata.
paras.en: [[9:4|And there stood up upon the step|Surrexerunt autem supra gradum]] the Levites who are named in the text, and [[9:5|said|dixerunt]]: [[9:5|Arise, bless the Lord your God from eternity to eternity|Surgite et benedicite Domino viventi, ab æterno et usque in æternum]] [Denis's text has *Domino viventi*, “the living Lord”, where the Vulgate has *Domino Deo vestro*], whom the elect bless in time in the present life and eternally in the life to come; [[9:5|and blessed be|et benedicant]] by all rational creatures the [[9:5|name of thy glory|nomini gloriæ tuæ]], that is, Thou Thyself, the glorious, [[9:5|high|excelso]], that is, dwelling in the highest heaven; or: let them do it with lofty devotion. Hence the angels too, when Christ was born of the Virgin, sang: [[Luke 2:14|Glory to God in the highest|Gloria in excelsis Deo]] [the Latin has *in excelsis*, the word Denis has just glossed in *excelso*]. [[9:5|with all blessing|In omni benedictione]], that is, with a full and perfect commendation of Thy goodness and perfection in itself, [[9:5|and praise|et laude]] of the same because of its works and benefits, or by its relation and bearing to created things.

paras.t: Porro quod subditur, Et dixit Esdras, non est de textu, sed subintelligitur, secundum eos qui dicunt totum residuum esse verbum ipsius Esdræ. Alii dicunt non esse subintelligendum, nec verba sequentia esse solius Esdræ, sed aliorum quoque confitentium Deo. Potius tamen apparet quod sint a solo Esdra prolata, approbantibus aliis. Non enim videtur quod plures simul protulerunt verba ista, sicut tres Pueri in camino quasi ex uno ore Deum laudabant.
paras.en: Further, what is added, And Esdras said [these words stand at this place in some texts but not in the Clementine Vulgate], is not of the text, but is understood, according to those who say that all the rest is the word of Esdras himself. Others say that it is not to be understood, and that the words that follow are not of Esdras alone but also of the others confessing to God. Yet it seems rather that they were spoken by Esdras alone, the others approving. For it does not appear that several spoke these words together, as the three Children in the furnace praised God as with one mouth[[Dan 3:51||]].

paras.t: Tu ipse, Domine, solus: quoniam solus es Deus verus, non plures dii; tu fecisti cœlum, id est omnes orbes cœlestes contentos sub summo cœlo, et cœlum cœlorum, id est cœlum empyreum quod ambit et continet cuncta creata: estque immobile et mansio Beatorum; dictum empyreum, id est igneum, non a calore, sed splendore; et omnem exercitum eorum, id est cunctos ordines supernorum spirituum. Interdum vero planetæ ac sidera vocantur cœli militia: unde quarto libro Regum legitur Manasses adorasse omnem militiam cœli. Juxta quem modum possent dici exercitus cœli ac orbium. Terram et universa quæ in ea sunt: quæ sunt creata et facta a Deo, tanquam a prima causa mediate vel immediate; maria et omnia quæ in eis sunt; et tu vivificas omnia hæc. Non est hoc intelligendum juxta quorumdam insaniam, quod totus mundus sit unum animal, cujus partes sint quatuor elementa, et reliqua animata sint, vel quod Deus sit anima mundi aut omnium vita formalis; sed omnia hæc, id est quædam de his omnibus, vivificat Deus, aut certe metaphorice vivificat omnia, dando singulis aliquam operationem, motum seu inclinationem ad proprium finem. Vivum namque vocatur, quod movet se ipsum. Et exercitus cœli, id est universitas cœlestium civium, te adorat. Qui autem dicunt corpora cœlestia esse animata, affirmant exercitum cœli, id est universitatem planetarum, stellarum, orbiumque cœlestium Deum proprie adorare. Et quamvis dicantur non esse animata, attamen adorant Deum materialiter, quoniam sua eminentia, claritate et perfectione ostendunt Creatorem suum esse adorandum. Juxta quem modum cuncta creata Deum benedicere et laudare dicuntur.
paras.en: [[9:6|Thou thyself, O Lord alone|Tu ipse, Domine, solus]]: for Thou alone art the true God, not many gods; [[9:6|thou hast made heaven|tu fecisti cœlum]], that is, all the heavenly spheres contained beneath the highest heaven, [[9:6|and the heaven of heavens|et cœlum cœlorum]], that is, the empyrean heaven, which surrounds and contains all created things: it is unmoving and the dwelling of the Blessed, and is called empyrean, that is, fiery, not from its heat but from its splendour; [[9:6|and all the host thereof|et omnem exercitum eorum]], that is, all the orders of the heavenly spirits. Sometimes, however, the planets and stars are called the host of heaven: hence in the fourth book of Kings we read that Manasses [[4 Kings 21:3|adored all the host of heaven|adorasse omnem militiam cœli]]. In this way one could speak of the host of the heaven and of the spheres. [[9:6|the earth and all things that are in it|Terram et universa quæ in ea sunt]], which are created and made by God as by the first cause, mediately or immediately; [[9:6|the seas and all that are therein|maria et omnia quæ in eis sunt]]; [[9:6|and thou givest life to all these things|et tu vivificas omnia hæc]]. This is not to be understood according to the madness of certain people, that the whole world is one animal whose parts are the four elements, and that the other things are animate, or that God is the soul of the world or the formal life of all things; but God gives life to all these things, that is, to some of all these, or certainly He gives life to all things metaphorically, by giving to each some operation, motion or inclination to its proper end. For that is called living which moves itself. [[9:6|and the host of heaven|Et exercitus cœli]], that is, the whole company of the citizens of heaven, [[9:6|adoreth thee|te adorat]]. Those, however, who say that the heavenly bodies are animate affirm that the host of heaven, that is, the whole company of the planets, the stars and the heavenly spheres, properly adores God. And although they are said not to be animate, yet they adore God materially, since by their eminence, brightness and perfection they show that their Creator is to be adored. In this way all created things are said to bless and praise God[[Dan 3:57||]].

paras.t: Tu elegisti Abram per prædestinationem ab æterno, et tempore præordinato vocasti eum ad tuum obsequium, atque ad terram promissam. Hinc subditur: Et eduxisti eum de igne Chaldæorum. In Genesi legitur Abram exisse de Ur Chaldæorum: ubi per Ur, secundum quosdam, intelligitur villa seu locus nativitatis habitationisque Abram in Chaldæa. Alii asserunt per Ur intelligi ignem, dicentes ipsum Abram fuisse projectum in ignem de præcepto Nemrod, eo quod ignem noluerit adorare, et quod divina virtute exivit illæsus de igne. Cui dicto videtur hæc littera consonare. Posset tamen per ignem, tribulatio magna quam in Chaldæa toleravit, intelligi. Unde dicit Judith: Abraham tentatus est, et per multas tribulationes probatus, Dei amicus effectus est. Et posuisti nomen ejus Abraham, id est, eum qui antea vocabatur Abram, quod interpretatur pater excelsus, vocasti Abraham, quod interpretatur pater multarum gentium, dicens ad eum: Nec ultra vocabitur nomen tuum Abram, sed appellaberis Abraham, quia patrem multarum gentium constitui te.
paras.en: Thou [[9:7|chosest Abram|Tu elegisti Abram]] by predestination from eternity, and at the time ordained beforehand Thou didst call him to Thy service, and to the promised land. Hence it is added: [[9:7|and broughtest him forth out of the fire of the Chaldeans|Et eduxisti eum de igne Chaldæorum]]. In Genesis we read that Abram went out of Ur of the Chaldees[[Gen 11:31||]]: where by Ur, according to some, is understood the town or place of Abram's birth and dwelling in Chaldea. Others assert that by Ur is understood fire [Hebrew *ur*, “fire” or “light”], saying that Abram himself was thrown into the fire by order of Nemrod because he would not adore fire, and that by divine power he came out of the fire unharmed. This text seems to agree with that saying. Yet by fire may also be understood the great tribulation that he endured in Chaldea. Hence Judith says: [[Jdt 8:22|Abraham was tempted, and being proved by many tribulations, was made the friend of God|Abraham tentatus est, et per multas tribulationes probatus, Dei amicus effectus est]]. [[9:7|and gavest him the name of Abraham|Et posuisti nomen ejus Abraham]], that is, him who was before called Abram, which is interpreted *high father*, Thou didst call Abraham, which is interpreted *father of many nations*, saying to him: [[Gen 17:5|Neither shall thy name be called any more Abram: but thou shalt be called Abraham: because I have made thee a father of many nations|Nec ultra vocabitur nomen tuum Abram, sed appellaberis Abraham, quia patrem multarum gentium constitui te]].

paras.t: Et invenisti cor ejus fidele coram te. Quia in adversis et prosperis tibi constanter adhæsit, et fuit in fide præcipuus, qui contra spem in spem credidit.
paras.en: [[9:8|And thou didst find his heart faithful before thee|Et invenisti cor ejus fidele coram te]]. For in adversity and in prosperity he clung to Thee steadfastly, and was outstanding in faith, he [[Rom 4:18|who against hope believed in hope|qui contra spem in spem credidit]].

paras.t: Et vidisti afflictionem patrum nostrorum in Ægypto, dicens ad Moysen: Vidi afflictionem populi mei in Ægypto, et clamorem ejus audivi; et sciens dolorem ejus, descendi ut liberarem eum. Clamorem eorum audisti super mare Rubrum: juxta illud Exodi, Clamaverunt filii Israel ad Dominum.
paras.en: [[9:9|And thou sawest the affliction of our fathers in Egypt|Et vidisti afflictionem patrum nostrorum in Ægypto]], saying to Moses: [[Ex 3:7|I have seen the affliction of my people in Egypt, and I have heard their cry|Vidi afflictionem populi mei in Ægypto, et clamorem ejus audivi]]; [[Ex 3:8|And knowing their sorrow, I am come down to deliver them|et sciens dolorem ejus, descendi ut liberarem eum]]. [[9:9|and thou didst hear their cry by the Red Sea|Clamorem eorum audisti super mare Rubrum]], according to that of Exodus: The children of Israel [[Ex 14:10|cried to the Lord|Clamaverunt filii Israel ad Dominum]].

paras.t: Ad montem quoque Sinai descendisti: non locum mutando, sed mirabilia ibi agendo; et per creaturam subjectam, quia per angelum in tua persona apparentem et loquentem apparuisti. Propterea subditur: et locutus es cum eis de cœlo aerio. Quamvis enim angelus loqueretur Moysi tantum, non populo, decem tamen præcepta Dominus per angelum dedit, et protulit toto illo populo audiente, sicut in Exodo et Deuteronomio legitur. Unde Moyses ait ad populum: Interroga si facta est aliquando hujusmodi res, aut unquam cognitum, ut audiret populus vocem Dei loquentis de medio ignis, sicut tu audisti.
paras.en: [[9:13|Thou camest down also to mount Sinai|Ad montem quoque Sinai descendisti]][[Ex 19:18||]][[Ex 19:20||]]: not by changing place, but by working wonders there; and through a subject creature, since Thou didst appear through an angel appearing and speaking in Thy person[[Acts 7:38||]]. Therefore it is added: [[9:13|and didst speak with them from heaven|et locutus es cum eis de cœlo]], the heaven of the air. For although the angel spoke to Moses only, not to the people, yet the Lord gave the ten commandments through the angel, and uttered them in the hearing of all that people, as we read in Exodus[[Ex 20:1||]][[Ex 20:22||]] and Deuteronomy. Hence Moses says to the people: [[Deut 4:32|Ask|Interroga]] [[Deut 4:32|if ever there was done the like thing, or it hath been known at any time|si facta est aliquando hujusmodi res, aut unquam cognitum]], [[Deut 4:33|That a people should hear the voice of God speaking out of the midst of fire, as thou hast heard|ut audiret populus vocem Dei loquentis de medio ignis, sicut tu audisti]].

paras.t: Et dedisti eis judicia recta, id est judicialia præcepta veraciter justa, et legem veritatis, id est legem Mosaicam, in qua nihil est falsitatis, et ea quæ credenda sunt, proponuntur, ac veritas de Deo et creaturis docetur, cærimonias, id est præcepta cærimonialia, et præcepta bona, videlicet præcepta moralia; et sabbatum sanctificatum ostendisti eis, jubendo ut diem septimum celebrarent.
paras.en: [[9:13|and thou gavest them right judgments|Et dedisti eis judicia recta]], that is, judicial precepts truly just, [[9:13|and the law of truth|et legem veritatis]], that is, the law of Moses, in which there is nothing false, and the things to be believed are set forth, and the truth about God and creatures is taught, [[9:13|ceremonies|cærimonias]], that is, ceremonial precepts, [[9:13|and good precepts|et præcepta bona]], namely moral precepts; [[9:14|Thou madest known to them thy holy sabbath|et sabbatum sanctificatum ostendisti eis]], commanding them to keep the seventh day[[Ex 20:8||]][[Ex 20:10||]].

paras.t: Ipsi vero et patres nostri superbe egerunt, per rebellionem contra te et Moysen, qui loquitur eis: Locutus sum, et non audistis; sed adversantes imperio Domini, et tumentes superbia, ascendistis in montem. Et dederunt caput, id est cor suum inclinaverunt, ut reverterentur ad servitutem suam pristinam in Ægypto, atque ad consuetum jugum diaboli, obsequiumque peccati, dicentes: Utinam pereamus, et non inducat nos Dominus in terram istam, ne cadamus gladio. Nonne melius est reverti in Ægyptum? Dixeruntque alter ad alterum: Constituamus nobis ducem, et revertamur in Ægyptum.
paras.en: [[9:16|But they and our fathers dealt proudly|Ipsi vero et patres nostri superbe egerunt]], by rebellion against Thee and against Moses, who says to them: [[Deut 1:43|I spoke, and you hearkened not: but resisting the commandment of the Lord, and swelling with pride, you went up into the mountain|Locutus sum, et non audistis; sed adversantes imperio Domini, et tumentes superbia, ascendistis in montem]]. [[9:17|and gave the head|Et dederunt caput]], that is, they bent their heart, [[9:17|to return to their bondage|ut reverterentur ad servitutem suam]] of old in Egypt, and to the accustomed yoke of the devil and the service of sin, saying: [[Num 14:3|would God we may die|Utinam pereamus]], [[Num 14:3|and that the Lord may not bring us into this land, lest we fall by the sword|et non inducat nos Dominus in terram istam, ne cadamus gladio]]. [[Num 14:3|Is it not better to return into Egypt?|Nonne melius est reverti in Ægyptum?]] [[Num 14:4|And they said one to another: Let us appoint a captain, and let us return into Egypt|Dixeruntque alter ad alterum: Constituamus nobis ducem, et revertamur in Ægyptum]].

paras.t: Et quidem quum fecissent sibi vitulum conflatilem, quia Aaron compulerant, ut per manum artificum formaret imaginem vituli; et dixissent: Iste est Deus tuus, o Israel, qui te eduxit de Ægypto. In Exodo leguntur dixisse: Hi sunt dii tui, Israel, qui te eduxerunt de terra Ægypti. Quomodo ergo hic narrantur in singulari dixisse, Hic est Deus tuus? Respondetur, quod ibi plurale pro singulari sumpserunt, ut sæpe fit in Scripturis. Feceruntque blasphemias magnas, sacrificantes idolo vano, et illud Deum vocando, atque in circuitu ejus choreas ducendo et concinendo, juxta quod legitur: Sedit populus manducare et bibere, et surrexerunt ludere.
paras.en: [[9:18|Yea when they had made also to themselves a molten calf|Et quidem quum fecissent sibi vitulum conflatilem]], for they had forced Aaron to fashion the image of a calf by the hands of craftsmen[[Ex 32:1||]], [[9:18|and had said|et dixissent]]: [[9:18|This is thy God|Iste est Deus tuus]], O Israel, [[9:18|that brought thee out of Egypt|qui te eduxit de Ægypto]]. In Exodus they are read to have said: [[Ex 32:4|These are thy gods, O Israel, that have brought thee out of the land of Egypt|Hi sunt dii tui, Israel, qui te eduxerunt de terra Ægypti]]. How then are they told here to have said in the singular, [[9:18|This is thy God|Hic est Deus tuus]]? The answer is that there they used the plural for the singular, as is often done in the Scriptures. [[9:18|and had committed great blasphemies|Feceruntque blasphemias magnas]], sacrificing to a vain idol and calling it God, and dancing round it and singing together, according to what we read: [[Ex 32:6|the people sat down to eat and drink, and they rose up to play|Sedit populus manducare et bibere, et surrexerunt ludere]][[1 Cor 10:7||]].

paras.t: Et spiritum tuum bonum dedisti, qui duceret eos: quod intelligi potest de angelo sancto, qui columnam nubis et ignis movendo rectum eis iter ostendit. Unde in Exodo Dominus dixit: Ecce ego mittam angelum meum, qui præcedat te et custodiat in via. Potest quoque intelligi de Spiritu Sancto, quem Dominus infudit Moysi ductori ipsorum, ut tam caritative et mansuete perduceret perversum populum illum: qui Spiritus per mirabilia multa ipsos præcessit. Nam in Exodo legitur Moyses exorasse: Si non tu ipse præcedas nos, ne educas nos de loco isto, etc. De quo Spiritu ait Propheta: Spiritus tuus bonus deducet me in terram rectam.
