paras.en: [[9:20|And thou gavest them thy good Spirit|Et spiritum tuum bonum dedisti]], to lead them [Denis's text reads *duceret*, “to lead”, where the Vulgate has *doceret*, “to teach”; the edition marks the word with a footnote giving a variant, only partly legible in the scan]: which can be understood of the holy angel, who by moving the pillar of cloud and of fire showed them the right way[[Ex 14:19||]] [the margin reference here cannot be read in the scan; Ex 14:19 fits the sense]. Hence in Exodus the Lord said: [[Ex 23:20|Behold I will send my angel, who shall go before thee, and keep thee in thy journey|Ecce ego mittam angelum meum, qui præcedat te et custodiat in via]]. It can also be understood of the Holy Spirit, whom the Lord poured into Moses their leader, so that he might lead that perverse people through so lovingly and so gently: and this Spirit went before them by many wonders. For in Exodus we read that Moses prayed: [[Ex 33:15|If thou thyself dost not go before, bring us not out of this place|Si non tu ipse præcedas nos, ne educas nos de loco isto]], etc. Of this Spirit the Prophet says: [[Ps 142:10|Thy good spirit shall lead me into the right land|Spiritus tuus bonus deducet me in terram rectam]].

paras.t: Nihilque eis defuit de necessariis vitæ. Interdum tamen ad tempus sustinuerunt penuriam, famem, sitim, sed misericorditer et celeriter eis providit. Vestimenta eorum non inveteraverunt, et pedes eorum non sunt attriti, id est læsi aut lassitudine afflicti. Hoc est quod in Deuteronomio scriptum est: Adduxit vos per desertum quadraginta annis; non sunt attrita vestimenta vestra, nec calceamenta pedum vestrorum vetustate consumpta sunt: quod fuit grande miraculum. Quod vero hic dicitur, Pedes eorum non sunt attriti, ponitur contentum pro continente. Vel intelligendum est de justis: quibus et manna sapuit sicut volebant, secundum illud Sapientiæ, Ad quod quisque volebat, convertebatur. Perversi autem fatigabantur, juxta illud Numerorum: Ortum est murmur populi quasi dolentium pro labore. Et rursus in libro eodem: Cœpit tædere populum itineris ac laboris.
paras.en: [[9:21|and nothing was wanting to them|Nihilque eis defuit]] of the necessaries of life. Sometimes, however, they suffered want, hunger and thirst for a time, but He provided for them mercifully and quickly. [[9:21|their garments did not grow old|Vestimenta eorum non inveteraverunt]], [[9:21|and their feet were not worn|et pedes eorum non sunt attriti]], that is, hurt or afflicted with weariness. This is what is written in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 29:5|He hath brought you forty years through the desert|Adduxit vos per desertum quadraginta annis]]: [[Deut 29:5|your garments are not worn out, neither are the shoes of your feet consumed with age|non sunt attrita vestimenta vestra, nec calceamenta pedum vestrorum vetustate consumpta sunt]]; which was a great miracle. But where it is said here, [[9:21|their feet were not worn|Pedes eorum non sunt attriti]], the thing contained is put for the thing containing [that is, the feet are named for the shoes that hold them]. Or it is to be understood of the just: to whom the manna also tasted as they wished, according to that of Wisdom: [[Wis 16:21|it was turned to what every man liked|Ad quod quisque volebat, convertebatur]]. But the perverse grew weary, according to that of Numbers: [[Num 11:1|there arose a murmuring of the people against the Lord, as it were repining at their fatigue|Ortum est murmur populi quasi dolentium pro labore]]. And again in the same book: [[Num 21:4|the people began to be weary of their journey and labour|Cœpit tædere populum itineris ac laboris]].

paras.t: Et dedisti eis regna, id est regiones, imo terras triginta unius regum, in terra promissionis, ut Josue dicit, et populos eis subjecisti.
paras.en: [[9:22|And thou gavest them kingdoms|Et dedisti eis regna]], that is, regions, indeed the lands of thirty-one kings in the land of promise, as Josue says[[Jos 12:24||]], [[9:22|and nations|et populos]] Thou didst subject to them.

paras.t: Provocaverunt autem te ad iracundiam: non concitando in te immaterialissimo Deo aliquam passionem, turbationem, aut alterationem, sed ad justæ ultionis effectum seu æquitatis rigorem, sicut per Jeremiam testatus es: Numquid me ad iracundiam provocant? nonne semetipsos in confusionem vultus sui?
paras.en: [[9:26|But they provoked thee to wrath|Provocaverunt autem te ad iracundiam]]: not by stirring up in Thee, the wholly immaterial God, any passion, disturbance or change, but to the effect of just vengeance, or the rigour of equity, as Thou didst testify through Jeremias: [[Jer 7:19|Do they provoke me to anger|Numquid me ad iracundiam provocant]]? [[Jer 7:19|is it not themselves, to the confusion of their own countenance?|nonne semetipsos in confusionem vultus sui?]]

paras.t: Et in tempore tribulationis suæ clamaverunt ad te, et dedisti eis salvatores. Hoc frequenter factum est tempore judicum, ut ex historia libri Judicum elucescit. Scriptum est enim: Suscitavit Dominus judices qui liberarent eos. Quumque suscitaret judices, flectebatur misericordia, et audiebat afflictorum gemitus, et liberabat eos de cæde vastantium.
paras.en: [[9:27|And in the time of their tribulation they cried to thee|Et in tempore tribulationis suæ clamaverunt ad te]], [[9:27|thou gavest them saviours|et dedisti eis salvatores]]. This was often done in the time of the judges[[Judg 3:9||]][[Judg 3:15||]][[Judg 6:7||]], as is clear from the history of the book of Judges. For it is written: [[Judg 2:16|the Lord raised up judges, to deliver them|Suscitavit Dominus judices qui liberarent eos]]. [[Judg 2:18|And when the Lord raised them up judges|Quumque suscitaret judices]], [[Judg 2:18|he was moved to mercy, and heard the groanings of the afflicted, and delivered them from the slaughter of the oppressors|flectebatur misericordia, et audiebat afflictorum gemitus, et liberabat eos de cæde vastantium]].

paras.t: Quumque requievissent, id est cessationem ab hostium impugnatione habuissent, reversi sunt ad pristina vitia ac pejora. Conversique sunt rursum ad te, vexatione eis intellectum præstante, et liberasti eos: quod sæpius accidit sub diversis judicibus. Hinc in libro Judicum inducitur: Quumque mortuus esset judex, revertebantur, et multa majora (id est pejora) faciebant.
paras.en: [[9:28|But after they had rest|Quumque requievissent]], that is, had a respite from the attacks of their enemies, [[9:28|they returned to do evil|reversi sunt]], going back to their former vices and to worse. [[9:28|Then they returned|Conversique sunt]] again to Thee, vexation giving them understanding[[Is 28:19||]], [[9:28|and deliveredst them|et liberasti eos]]: which happened many times under different judges. Hence it is set down in the book of Judges: [[Judg 2:19|But after the judge was dead, they returned, and did much worse things|Quumque mortuus esset judex, revertebantur, et multa majora (id est pejora) faciebant]] [Denis's text reads *multa majora (id est pejora)*, “many greater things (that is, worse)”; the Vulgate has *multo pejora*].

paras.t: Et dederunt humerum recedentem, id est onus præceptorum tuorum super se ferre recusaverunt, juxta illud Zachariæ: Noluerunt attendere, et averterunt scapulas recedentes. Cor suum posuerunt ut adamantem, ne audirent legem.
paras.en: [[9:29|and they withdrew the shoulder|Et dederunt humerum recedentem]] [literally *gave a shoulder drawing back*], that is, they refused to bear upon themselves the burden of Thy commandments, according to that of Zacharias: [[Zach 7:11|they would not hearken, and they turned away the shoulder to depart|Noluerunt attendere, et averterunt scapulas recedentes]]. [[Zach 7:12|And they made their heart as the adamant stone, lest they should hear the law|Cor suum posuerunt ut adamantem, ne audirent legem]].

paras.t: Et protraxisti, id est prolongasti, super eos annos multos, id est multis annis eorum punitionem et captivitatem distulisti, et contestatus es eos in spiritu tuo, id est per revelationem propheticam a Prophetis prolatam sub testimonio veritatis, prænuntiasti et comminatus es eis flagella et adversa instantia. Unde per Jeremiam sæpe locutus est: Misi ad vos omnes servos meos Prophetas, ut reverteretur unusquisque a via sua mala.
paras.en: [[9:30|And thou didst forbear with them|Et protraxisti]], that is, Thou didst prolong, [[9:30|for many years|super eos annos multos]], that is, Thou didst put off their punishment and captivity for many years, [[9:30|and didst testify against them by thy spirit|et contestatus es eos in spiritu tuo]], that is, by prophetic revelation uttered by the Prophets under the witness of truth, Thou didst foretell and threaten them with scourges and adversities at hand. Hence He often spoke through Jeremias: [[Jer 7:25|I have sent to you all my servants the prophets|Misi ad vos omnes servos meos Prophetas]], that every one might return from his evil way[[Jer 35:15||]].

paras.t: In misericordiis autem tuis plurimis non fecisti eos in consumptionem, id est ex magna et infinita misericordia tua noluisti eos omnino disperdere, exstirpare, exstinguere, sed reliquias reservasti ex eis: sicut in Ezechiele sæpe habetur. Unde per Jeremiam Dominus dixit: Castigo te in judicio, ut non tibi videaris innoxius; non autem te faciam in consummationem.
paras.en: [[9:31|Yet in thy very many mercies thou didst not utterly consume them|In misericordiis autem tuis plurimis non fecisti eos in consumptionem]], that is, out of Thy great and infinite mercy Thou wouldst not wholly destroy them, root them out and blot them out, but didst keep a remnant of them, as is often found in Ezechiel. Hence the Lord said through Jeremias: [[Jer 30:11|I will chastise thee in judgment, that thou mayst not seem to thyself innocent|Castigo te in judicio, ut non tibi videaris innoxius]]; [[Jer 30:11|but I will not utterly consume thee|non autem te faciam in consummationem]].

paras.t: Nunc itaque, Deus magne, fortis et terribilis, ne avertas a facie tua omnem laborem qui invenit nos: id est tribulationes, quas pro peccatis nostris incurrimus, misericorditer intuere, et per eas nobis ignosce, ac de cætero pacem et prosperitatem concede, quia post tempestatem facis tranquillum, et post fletum exsultationem infundis, et quum iratus fueris, misericordiæ recordaberis, nec vindicas bis in idipsum; a diebus regis Assur, id est regis Assyriorum, puta Sennacherib, qui valde vexavit sanctum regem Ezechiam et populum ejus. Filius quoque regis illius captivavit Manassen filium Ezechiæ, ut secundo libro Paralipomenon legitur.
paras.en: [[9:32|Now therefore our God, great, strong, and terrible|Nunc itaque, Deus magne, fortis et terribilis]], [[9:32|turn not away from thy face all the labour which hath come upon us|ne avertas a facie tua omnem laborem qui invenit nos]]: that is, look mercifully on the tribulations that we have incurred for our sins, and through them forgive us, and for the rest grant us peace and prosperity; for [[Tob 3:22|after a storm thou makest a calm, and after tears and weeping thou pourest in joyfulness|post tempestatem facis tranquillum, et post fletum exsultationem infundis]], and [[Hab 3:2|when thou art angry, thou wilt remember mercy|quum iratus fueris, misericordiæ recordaberis]], nor dost Thou punish twice for the same thing; [[9:32|from the days of the king of Assur|a diebus regis Assur]], that is, of the king of the Assyrians, namely Sennacherib, who sorely harassed the holy king Ezechias and his people[[4 Kings 18:13||]]. The son of that king also took captive Manasses, the son of Ezechias, as we read in the second book of Paralipomenon[[2 Par 33:11||]] [the margin gives I Par. xxxi, 11; the passage is 2 Par 33:11].

paras.t: Et ipsi in regnis suis, id est reges nostri in regionibus terræ promissionis, videlicet in Judæa, Galilæa, Samaria et aliis, non servierunt tibi, loquendo de regibus Israelitici populi multis, non omnibus.
paras.en: And they [[9:35|in their kingdoms|in regnis suis]], that is, our kings in the regions of the land of promise, namely in Judea, Galilee, Samaria and the others, [[9:35|have not served thee|non servierunt tibi]]: speaking of many of the kings of the people of Israel, not of all.

paras.t: Ecce nos ipsi hodie servi sumus, id est subjecti jugo regis Persarum, et tributarii, quantum ad vulgus. Et fruges ejus multiplicantur regibus quos posuisti super nos, id est blada terræ nostræ pro magna parte deveniunt in usum regum gentilium, qui præsident nobis, propter peccata nostra; et corporibus nostris dominantur et jumentis: quia oportet ut serviamus eis, quum jusserint, in propriis personis et cum nostris jumentis; mens tamen tali servituti non est obnoxia.
paras.en: [[9:36|Behold we ourselves this day are bondmen|Ecce nos ipsi hodie servi sumus]], that is, subject to the yoke of the king of the Persians, and tributaries [these words stand in Denis's text of the verse, not in the Clementine Vulgate], as regards the common people. [[9:37|And the fruits thereof grow up for the kings, whom thou hast set over us|Et fruges ejus multiplicantur regibus quos posuisti super nos]], that is, the corn [*blada*, a medieval word for crops of grain] of our land goes in great part to the use of the gentile kings who rule over us, [[9:37|for our sins|propter peccata nostra]]; [[9:37|and they have dominion over our bodies, and over our beasts|et corporibus nostris dominantur et jumentis]]: for we must serve them when they command, in our own persons and with our beasts; the mind, however, is not bound to such servitude.

paras.t: Super omnibus ergo his, etc., id est de omnibus prædictis peccatis firmiter proponimus nos emendare, et de hoc percutimus fœdus et scribimus, id est litteram testimonialem conficimus, et signant, id est sigilla apponunt pro se et populo, principes nostri, in testimonium veritatis, ut inexcusabiles inveniamur, nisi egerimus ita.
paras.en: [[9:38|And because of all this|Super omnibus ergo his]], etc., that is, we firmly purpose to amend ourselves of all the sins aforesaid, and of this we [[9:38|make a covenant|percutimus fœdus]] [[9:38|and write it|et scribimus]], that is, we draw up a letter of testimony, and [[9:38|sign it|signant]], that is, set their seals on it for themselves and the people, [[9:38|our princes|principes nostri]], in witness of the truth, so that we may be found without excuse unless we do so.

paras.t: Præterea possent hæc omnia spiritualiter interpretari; sed sicut litteralis horum sensus præhabitus est in Scripturis præallegatis, ita et eorumdem mysticus intellectus: ideo prolixitatem devitans, pertranseo. Sed pensemus, qualiter vexatio præstet intellectum auditui. Etenim quidam convertuntur ad Dominum, introeunt claustrum, obsequuntur Altissimo ex sincero bonitatis et virtutis affectu seu Dei intuitu et amore; quidam, desiderio præmii; alii, timore supplicii. Primum est optimum; secundum, commendabile; tertium, dispositivum ad promerendum.
paras.en: Moreover, all these things could be interpreted spiritually; but as their literal sense has been given beforehand in the Scriptures cited above, so has their mystical understanding too: therefore, to avoid length, I pass over it. But let us consider how [[Is 28:19|vexation alone shall make you understand what you hear|vexatio præstet intellectum auditui]]. For some turn to the Lord, enter the cloister and serve the Most High out of a sincere love of goodness and virtue, or for the regard and love of God; some out of desire for reward; others out of fear of punishment. The first is the best; the second, commendable; the third, a disposition towards meriting.

10.title: Declaratio capituli decimi: Signatores autem fuerunt Nehemias Athersatha filius Hachelai, etc.
10.title_en: Declaration of the tenth chapter: And the subscribers were Nehemias, Athersatha the son of Hachelai, etc.

paras.t: Signatores autem, id est sigillatores litteræ nostræ pactionis, de qua in fine præcedentis habetur capituli, fuerunt: Nehemias, qui alio nomine dictus est Athersatha: qui fuit sacerdos, sicut et ceteri in textu consequenter expressi, qui secum sigillaverunt. Deinde nominantur in littera Levitæ et capitanei signatores.
paras.en: [[10:1|And the subscribers|Signatores autem]], that is, the sealers of the writing of our covenant, of which we read at the end of the preceding chapter[[9:38||]], [[10:1|were Nehemiah|fuerunt: Nehemias]], who by another name was called [[10:1|Athersatha|Athersatha]]: who was a priest, as were the others named next in the text, who sealed with him. Then the Levites and the chief men who signed are named in the text.

paras.t: Ut ambularent, id est conversarentur, in lege Domini. Et explicantur quædam in singulari, quæ promiserunt servare, quum subditur: et ut non daremus filias nostras in uxores populo terræ, id est Samaritanis, ceterisve gentilibus. Secundum fuit, quod non emerent aliquid a gentibus, venalia sua portantibus in die sabbati, neque in alia die sanctificata, id est solenni. Et hoc est quod dicitur: Populi quoque terræ qui important venalia, non accipiemus ab eis sabbato, etc. Cur ergo Christiani suas mercationes non relinquunt diebus dominicis et festivis? Dimittemus annum septimum, id est, agros nostros non seminabimus saltem ad proprium usum tantum septimo anno, juxta illud Levitici: Sex annis seres agrum tuum, et sex annis putabis vineam tuam, et colliges fructus ejus. Septimo anno sabbatum erit terræ requietionis Domini: agrum non seres, et vineam non putabis.
paras.en: [[10:29|That they would walk|Ut ambularent]], that is, live, [[10:29|in the law of God|in lege Domini]]. And certain things which they promised to keep are set out one by one, when it is added: [[10:30|And that we would not give our daughters|et ut non daremus filias nostras]] as wives [[10:30|to the people of the land|populo terræ]], that is, to the Samaritans or the other Gentiles. The second was that they would buy nothing from the Gentiles who brought their wares for sale on the sabbath day, nor on any other sanctified, that is, solemn, day. And this is what is said: [[10:31|the people of the land bring in things to sell|Populi quoque terræ qui important venalia]], [[10:31|that we would not buy them on the sabbath|non accipiemus ab eis sabbato]], etc. Why then do Christians not leave off their trading on Sundays and feast days? [[10:31|And that we would leave the seventh year|Dimittemus annum septimum]], that is, we will not sow our fields, at least for our own use only, in the seventh year, according to that saying of Leviticus: [[Lev 25:3|Six years thou shalt sow thy field and six years thou shalt prune thy vineyard, and shalt gather the fruits thereof|sex annis putabis vineam tuam, et colliges fructus ejus]]. [[Lev 25:4|in the seventh year there shall be a sabbath to the land, of the resting of the Lord. Thou shalt not sow thy field, nor prune thy vineyard|Septimo anno sabbatum erit terræ requietionis Domini: agrum non seres, et vineam non putabis]].

paras.t: Et statuemus super nos præcepta, hoc est, observantiis præceptorum subjiciemus corda nostra, et demus tertiam partem sicli per annum, id est, quolibet anno quivis qui habet, offerat tertiam partem sicli: quæ pecunia colligebatur die sequente ultimam diem festi Tabernaculorum, sicut istud expositum est supra.
paras.en: [[10:32|And we made ordinances for ourselves|Et statuemus super nos præcepta]], that is, we will subject our hearts to the observance of the commandments, [[10:32|to give the third part of a sicle every year|et demus tertiam partem sicli per annum]], that is, every year whoever has the means is to offer the third part of a sicle: which money was collected on the day following the last day of the feast of Tabernacles[[8:18||]], as was explained above.

paras.t: Sortes ergo misimus super oblationem lignorum inter sacerdotes et Levitas et populum, ut inferrent in domum Dei nostri; id est, per sortium eventum quæsivimus determinationem et certificationem, quis, quando et qualiter deberet adducere ligna, quibus nutriendus fuit ignis in altari holocaustorum jugiter ardens: quæ ligna apponere igni, ad sacerdotes spectabat, juxta illud: Ignis in altari semper ardebit, quem nutriet sacerdos, subjiciens ligna mane per singulos dies. Levitæ vero sacerdotibus subserviebant. Adducere autem ligna ad hoc, fuit Nathinæorum officium, ut legitur in Josue libro; sed solutio pretii pro hujusmodi lignis, pertinebat ad populum.
paras.en: [[10:34|And we cast lots among the priests, and the Levites, and the people for the offering of wood, that it might be brought into the house of our God|Sortes ergo misimus super oblationem lignorum inter sacerdotes et Levitas et populum, ut inferrent in domum Dei nostri]]; that is, by the outcome of lots we sought a settled and certain decision as to who should bring the wood, and when and how, with which the fire burning continually on the altar of holocausts was to be fed: and it fell to the priests to put this wood on the fire, according to that saying: [[Lev 6:12|the fire on the altar shall always burn, and the priest shall feed it, putting wood on it every day in the morning|Ignis in altari semper ardebit, quem nutriet sacerdos, subjiciens ligna mane per singulos dies]]. The Levites, for their part, served the priests. But bringing the wood for this was the office of the Nathinites, as we read in the book of Josue[[Jos 9:21||]][[Jos 9:27||]] [the margin's verse numbers are hard to read; Josue 9 tells how the Gabaonites were made hewers of wood for the altar]; while paying the price of such wood belonged to the people.

paras.t: Et ut afferremus primogenita terræ nostræ, id est, primos seu primitivos fructus agrorum nostrorum adduceremus ad offerendum hos Domino: quemadmodum in Levitico et Deuteronomio legitur; et primitiva fructus omnis ligni, id est primos arborum fructus qui erant Domino offerendi, et primitiva filiorum nostrorum. Primogeniti enim omnium tribuum Israel, dempta tribu Levi, offerebantur Deo in templo, et statim redimebantur pretio. Nempe ex tempore quo Dominus percussit omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti, sanctificavit sibi seu offerri deputavit omne primogenitum filiorum Israel, tam in hominibus quam in jumentis, prout in Exodo legitur. Et pecorum nostrorum. Primogenita enim pecorum secundum legem offeribilium, immolabantur, atque in usum sacerdotum venerunt. Primogenitum autem asini interficiebatur, vel ove commutabatur. Sed primogenita canum occidebantur, et ceterorum animalium primogenita pretio redimebantur. Et primitias ciborum nostrorum et libaminum, id est potuum, et decimam partem terræ nostræ, id est terræ nascentium, dabimus Levitis: qui sustentabantur decimis, sicut sacerdotes sacrificiis.
paras.en: [[10:35|And that we would bring the firstfruits of our land|Et ut afferremus primogenita terræ nostræ]], that is, that we would bring the first or earliest fruits of our fields to offer them to the Lord: as we read in Leviticus[[Lev 23:10||]] and Deuteronomy[[Deut 26:2||]]; [[10:35|and the firstfruits of all fruit of every tree|et primitiva fructus omnis ligni]], that is, the first fruits of the trees, which were to be offered to the Lord, [[10:36|And the firstborn of our sons|et primitiva filiorum nostrorum]]. For the firstborn of all the tribes of Israel, the tribe of Levi excepted, were offered to God in the temple, and at once redeemed for a price. For indeed, from the time when the Lord struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, he sanctified to himself, that is, appointed to be offered, every firstborn of the children of Israel, both of men and of beasts, as we read in Exodus[[Ex 13:2||]]. [[10:36|and of our cattle|Et pecorum nostrorum]]. For the firstborn of the cattle that might be offered according to the law were sacrificed, and went to the use of the priests[[Num 18:17||]][[Num 18:18||]]. But the firstborn of an ass was killed, or exchanged for a sheep[[Ex 13:13||]]. The firstborn of dogs, however, were killed[[Deut 23:18||]] [the margin seems to read Deut. xxi, 13, which does not fit; perhaps Deut 23:18, which forbids offering the price of a dog in the house of the Lord], and the firstborn of the other animals were redeemed for a price[[Num 18:15||]]. [[10:37|And that we would bring the firstfruits of our meats, and of our libations|Et primitias ciborum nostrorum et libaminum]], that is, of drinks, [[10:37|and the tithes of our ground|et decimam partem terræ nostræ]], that is, of what springs from the ground, we will give [[10:37|to the Levites|Levitis]]: who were maintained by the tithes, as the priests were by the sacrifices.

paras.t: Erit autem sacerdos de filiis Aaron, cum Levitis in decimis Levitarum, id est, aliquis sacerdos ex semine Aaron natus aderit, dum Levitæ a populo accipiunt decimas; et Levitæ offerent decimam partem decimæ suæ. Levitæ namque solvebant decimam decimarum pontifici, id est decimam partem decimarum eis a populo præstitarum.
paras.en: [[10:38|And the priest the son of Aaron shall be with the Levites in the tithes of the Levites|Erit autem sacerdos de filiis Aaron, cum Levitis in decimis Levitarum]], that is, some priest born of the seed of Aaron shall be present when the Levites receive the tithes from the people[[Num 18:21||]]; [[10:38|and the Levites shall offer the tithe of their tithes|et Levitæ offerent decimam partem decimæ suæ]]. For the Levites paid the tithe of the tithes to the high priest[[Num 18:26||]][[Num 18:28||]], that is, the tenth part of the tithes given to them by the people.

11.title: Expositio capituli undecimi: Habitaverunt autem principes populi in Jerusalem
11.title_en: Exposition of the eleventh chapter: And the princes of the people dwelt at Jerusalem

paras.t: Recitatur hic, qualiter civitas Jerusalem reædificata, fuerit populata. Habitaverunt autem principes populi in Jerusalem, id est, principales Judæorum in ipsa metropoli habitaverunt: qui erant aptiores defendere eam ab hostibus, qui in circuitu morabantur, et eam demoliri optabant, ac sæpius infestabant. Reliqua vero plebs de tribubus Juda, Levi ac Benjamin, misit sortem, ut tolleret unam partem de decem, id est, de decem viris unus moraretur in urbe Jerusalem, novem vero partes, id est ceteri, habitarent in civitatibus Judæ. Benedixit autem populus omnibus viris, qui se sponte obtulerant ut habitarent in Jerusalem: quoniam periculosius fuit habitare in ea, eo quod gentiles per gyrum specialiter conarentur ipsam Jerusalem devastare: ideo populus commendavit eos, et bona ipsis imprecabatur, qui voluntarie elegerunt commorari in ea.
paras.en: Here it is related how the city of Jerusalem, once rebuilt, was peopled. [[11:1|And the princes of the people dwelt at Jerusalem|Habitaverunt autem principes populi in Jerusalem]], that is, the leading men of the Jews dwelt in the capital itself: for they were the better able to defend it against the enemies who lived round about, who longed to pull it down and often harassed it. [[11:1|but the rest of the people|Reliqua vero plebs]] of the tribes of Juda, Levi and Benjamin [[11:1|cast lots, to take one part in ten|misit sortem, ut tolleret unam partem de decem]], that is, that one man in ten should stay in the city of Jerusalem, [[11:1|and nine parts|novem vero partes]], that is, the rest, should dwell [[11:1|in the other cities|in civitatibus]] of Juda. [[11:2|And the people blessed all the men that willingly offered themselves to dwell in Jerusalem|Benedixit autem populus omnibus viris, qui se sponte obtulerant ut habitarent in Jerusalem]]: since it was more dangerous to live there, because the Gentiles round about strove especially to lay Jerusalem itself waste, the people therefore praised them, and called down blessings on those who chose of their own will to live in it.

paras.t: Habitavit autem unusquisque in possessione sua in urbibus Israel, sacerdotes, Levitæ, Nathinæi, et filii servorum Salomonis. Istud exponitur de prætactis jam hominibus, qui non erant necessarii ad populationem custodiamque Jerusalem: ideo permissi sunt habitare in oppidis, in quibus vel ipsi, vel patres eorum antea habitaverunt. Quod etiam intelligendum est de Israelitis natis ex novem tribubus, qui manus evaserunt Assyriorum, et ad Ezechiam confugerunt, ac postmodum cum populo regni Juda a Chaldæis capti fuerunt: quorum posteri redierunt cum populo Juda a Babylonica captivitate, nec compulsi sunt in Jerusalem habitare.
paras.en: [[11:3|And every one dwelt in his possession|Habitavit autem unusquisque in possessione sua]], [[11:3|in their cities: Israel, the priests, the Levites, the Nathinites, and the children of the servants of Solomon|in urbibus Israel, sacerdotes, Levitæ, Nathinæi, et filii servorum Salomonis]]. This is to be understood of the men already mentioned, who were not needed for peopling and guarding Jerusalem: so they were allowed to dwell in the towns in which they themselves or their fathers had lived before. The same is to be understood of the Israelites born of the nine tribes, who escaped the hands of the Assyrians and fled to Ezechias, and were afterwards taken by the Chaldeans together with the people of the kingdom of Juda: their descendants returned with the people of Juda from the Babylonian captivity, and were not compelled to dwell in Jerusalem.

paras.t: Et in Jerusalem habitaverunt de filiis Juda et de filiis Benjamin hi qui exprimuntur in textu, qui expositione non indiget, quantum ad illos. Deinde nominantur sacerdotes et Levitæ, qui in Jerusalem habitaverunt.
paras.en: [[11:4|And in Jerusalem there dwelt some of the children of Juda, and some of the children of Benjamin|Et in Jerusalem habitaverunt de filiis Juda et de filiis Benjamin]] those who are named in the text, which needs no explanation as far as they are concerned. Then the priests and Levites who dwelt in Jerusalem are named.

paras.t: Et episcopus Levitarum in Jerusalem, Azzi filius Bani. Vir iste vocatur episcopus Levitarum per participationem episcopalis officii, et quantum ad id a quo nomen imponitur. Episcopus namque dicitur quasi superintendens: et sic iste fuit specialiter præfectus Levitis, tanquam eorum præpositus et provisor. Nec fuit pontifex Judæorum. De filiis Asaph erant cantores in ministerio domus Dei. Asaph quippe fuerat unus principalium cantorum a David institutorum, ut primo Paralipomenon scriptum est. Ideo posteri ejus fuerunt cantores in cultu templi et laudibus Dei. Præceptum quippe regis super eos erat: id est, ex ordinatione et jussione David regis antiqua, debebant sic esse dispositi et psallentes; et ordo in cantoribus per singulos dies, id est, cantores successive in vice et ordine suo suum fecerunt officium ordinate. Et Phathahia in manu regis, id est secundum prætactam David regis institutionem, juxta omne verbum populi, id est, secundum quod populus approbaverat, ut juxta sortium eventum habitarent, et suum officium exercerent in Jerusalem.
paras.en: [[11:22|And the overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem, was Azzi the son of Bani|Et episcopus Levitarum in Jerusalem, Azzi filius Bani]]. This man is called the bishop of the Levites [the Latin *episcopus*, which the Douay-Rheims renders "overseer", is the word for a bishop] by a share in the episcopal office, and with regard to that from which the name is given. For a bishop is so called as being one who oversees: and so this man was set especially over the Levites, as their superior and provider. Nor was he the high priest of the Jews. [[11:22|Of the sons of Asaph, were the singing men in the ministry of the house of God|De filiis Asaph erant cantores in ministerio domus Dei]]. For Asaph had been one of the chief singers appointed by David, as is written in the first book of Paralipomenon[[1 Par 16:5||]][[1 Par 16:7||]]. Therefore his descendants were singers in the worship of the temple and in the praises of God. [[11:23|For the king's commandment was concerning them|Præceptum quippe regis super eos erat]]: that is, by the ancient ordinance and command of King David they were to be so arranged and to sing psalms; [[11:23|and an order among the singing men day by day|et ordo in cantoribus per singulos dies]], that is, the singers did their office in due order, one after another, each in his turn and course. [[11:24|And Phathahia|Et Phathahia]] was [[11:24|at the hand of the king|in manu regis]], that is, according to the ordinance of King David mentioned before, [[11:24|in all matters concerning the people|juxta omne verbum populi]], that is, according to what the people had approved: that they should dwell as the lots fell, and carry out their office in Jerusalem.

paras.t: De filiis Juda, etc. Hic nominantur urbes ad tribum Juda pertinentes, in quibus reliqui de tribu illa habitaverunt. Filii autem Benjamin, etc. Hic idem ostenditur de Benjamin tribu, quia exprimuntur hic urbes tribus illius, in quibus habitaverunt filii Benjamin, qui in Jerusalem non sunt commorati. Et de Levitis partitiones Judæ et Benjamin, id est, Levitæ et sacerdotes non deputati habitare in Jerusalem, manserunt in civitatibus tribuum Juda ac Benjamin: quæ sequestratæ et assignatæ fuerunt sub Josue pro habitatione sacerdotum ac Levitarum, ut legitur in Josue codice.
paras.en: [[11:25|Of the children of Juda|De filiis Juda]], etc. Here are named the cities belonging to the tribe of Juda, in which the rest of that tribe dwelt. [[11:31|And the children of Benjamin|Filii autem Benjamin]], etc. Here the same is shown of the tribe of Benjamin, for here are named the cities of that tribe in which those children of Benjamin dwelt who did not live in Jerusalem. [[11:36|And of the Levites were portions of Juda and Benjamin|Et de Levitis portiones Judæ et Benjamin.]], that is, the Levites and priests not appointed to dwell in Jerusalem remained in the cities of the tribes of Juda and Benjamin, which were set apart and assigned under Josue for the dwelling of the priests and Levites, as we read in the book of Josue[[Jos 21:1||]].

12.title: Expositio capituli duodecimi: Hi sunt autem sacerdotes et Levitæ qui ascenderunt
12.title_en: Exposition of the twelfth chapter: Now these are the priests and the Levites, that went up

paras.t: Dedicatio civitatis Jerusalem et murorum ejus, describitur hic. Fuit enim hæc civitas Deo specialiter consecranda et ejus cultui deputata, quia in ea fuit studium legis, templum et loca sacrificiorum ac divini obsequii, habitatio sacerdotum præcipuorum ac principum. Et quia dedicatio illa facta est multum solenniter, confluentibus ad eamdem universis sacerdotibus ac Levitis, idcirco præmittitur sermo de sacerdotibus et Levitis, a principio ex licentia regis Cyri reversis.
paras.en: The dedication of the city of Jerusalem and of its walls is described here. For this city was to be consecrated to God in a special way and set apart for his worship, since in it were the study of the law, the temple and the places of sacrifice and of divine service, and the dwelling of the chief priests and princes. And because that dedication was carried out very solemnly, all the priests and Levites flocking to it, an account is first given of the priests and Levites who returned at the beginning by leave of King Cyrus.

paras.t: Hi sunt autem sacerdotes et Levitæ qui ascenderunt de Babylonia ad Judæam cum Zorobabel: Josue, id est Jesus pontifex, filius Josedec pontificis: qui Josedec (ut primo Paralipomenon legitur) a Chaldæis ductus est in Babylonem, ejusque filius Josue cum Zorobabel rediit, et pontificis officio functus est; Saraa, Jeremias, Esdras, quem aliqui dicunt esse hunc Esdram auctorem libri præcedentis, dicentes quod primo rediit cum Zorobabel, postea ad regem Persarum redierit pro pluribus Judæis reducendis et pro privilegiis impetrandis. Alii potius opinantur, quod iste sit alius Esdras: quia verisimile est, quod illum Esdram Scriptura statim nominasset post Josue pontificem, et quod in descriptione eorum qui cum Zorobabel redierunt, ipse fuisset nominatim expressus: quod non est factum, ut patet in libro Esdræ. Et de hac re dictum est supra in Esdræ expositione. Isti principes sacerdotum, non quod omnes fuerint pontifices, sed Josue tantum tempore illo. Ideo principes sacerdotum dicuntur, id est principales inter sacerdotes: sicut et David sub pontifice ordinavit viginti quatuor sacerdotes majores, prout primo Paralipomenon continetur. Et fratres eorum, sacerdotes minus principales, in diebus Josue pontificis memorati. Porro Levitæ, qui redierunt cum Zorobabel, fuerunt Jesua, et ceteri qui exprimuntur in littera.
paras.en: [[12:1|Now these are the priests and the Levites, that went up|Hi sunt autem sacerdotes et Levitæ qui ascenderunt]] from Babylon to Judea [[12:1|with Zorobabel|cum Zorobabel]]: [[12:1|Josue|Josue]], that is, Jesus the high priest, son of Josedec the high priest: which Josedec (as we read in the first book of Paralipomenon[[1 Par 6:15||]]) was led away into Babylon by the Chaldeans, and his son Josue returned with Zorobabel and discharged the office of high priest; [[12:1|Saraia, Jeremias, Esdras|Saraa, Jeremias, Esdras]], whom some say is this Esdras, the author of the preceding book, saying that he first returned with Zorobabel, and afterwards went back to the king of the Persians to bring back more of the Jews and to obtain privileges. Others rather think that this is another Esdras: for it is likely that Scripture would have named that Esdras straight after Josue the high priest, and that in the list of those who returned with Zorobabel he would have been named expressly: which was not done, as is plain in the book of Esdras[[1 Esd 2:2||]]. And this matter was spoken of above, in the exposition of Esdras. [[12:7|These were the chief of the priests|Isti principes sacerdotum]]: not that all were high priests, but only Josue at that time. So they are called chief of the priests, that is, the principal men among the priests: as David too, under the high priest, appointed twenty-four greater priests, as is contained in the first book of Paralipomenon[[1 Par 24:1||]]. [[12:7|and of their brethren|Et fratres eorum]], the less principal priests, [[12:7|in the days of Josue|in diebus Josue]], the high priest mentioned. [[12:8|And the Levites|Porro Levitæ]] who returned with Zorobabel were [[12:8|Jesua|Jesua]], and the others who are named in the text.

paras.t: Consequenter linea generationis sacerdotum describitur. Josue autem pontifex genuit Joachim, quem Judith vocat Eliachim, sub quo et historia Judith creditur contigisse. Et Joachim genuit Eliasib, de quo dictum est ante; fuitque pontifex tempore quo Nehemias cœpit muros Jerusalem reædificare. Et Eliasib genuit Joiada, quem Josephus vocat Judam, quia binomius fuit. Et Joiada genuit Jonathan, qui a Josepho Joannes vocatur: de quo forsan intelligendum est illud Machabæorum, Orationem faciebant sacerdotes, Jonatha inchoante, quando et Nehemias specialem fecit orationem, ut secundo Machabæorum libro habetur. Et Jonathan genuit Jeddoa, quem Josephus nominat Jaddum: qui Jaddus, secundum eumdem, obviavit in pontificalibus Alexandro Magno, ut suo loco Deo præstante narrabitur.
paras.en: Next the line of descent of the priests is described. [[12:10|And Josue begot Joacim|Josue autem pontifex genuit Joachim]], whom Judith calls Eliachim[[Jdt 4:5||]][[Jdt 4:7||]], under whom the story of Judith is also believed to have taken place. [[12:10|and Joacim begot Eliasib|Et Joachim genuit Eliasib]], of whom we spoke before[[3:1||]]; and he was high priest at the time when Nehemias began to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem. [[12:10|and Eliasib begot Joiada|Et Eliasib genuit Joiada]], whom Josephus calls Judas, because he had two names. [[12:11|And Joiada begot Jonathan|Et Joiada genuit Jonathan]], who is called John by Josephus: of whom perhaps that saying of the Machabees is to be understood: [[2 Mach 1:23|the priests made prayer|Orationem faciebant sacerdotes]], [[2 Mach 1:23|Jonathan beginning|Jonatha inchoante]], when Nehemias too made a special prayer, as we find in the second book of Machabees[[2 Mach 1:24||]]. [[12:11|and Jonathan begot Jeddoa|Et Jonathan genuit Jeddoa]], whom Josephus names Jaddus: which Jaddus, according to the same writer [Josephus, Antiquities XI, 8, as the margin notes], went out in his pontifical robes to meet Alexander the Great, as will be told in its place, God granting.

paras.t: In diebus autem Joachim pontificis jam præfati, erant sacerdotes (qui fuerunt et principes familiarum, id est præcipui sacerdotalium familiarum) qui exprimuntur in textu.
paras.en: [[12:12|And in the days of Joacim|In diebus autem Joachim]], the high priest already mentioned, [[12:12|the priests|erant sacerdotes]] (who were also [[12:12|heads of the families|principes familiarum]], that is, the foremost men of the priestly families) were those who are named in the text.

paras.t: Levitæ in diebus, id est tempore pontificatus, Eliasib, et Joiada, et Johanan, qui paulo ante vocatus est Jonathan, et Jeddoa, scripti principes familiarum, id est descripti principales in familiis Leviticis, quæ ab eis duxerunt originem: quorum descriptio non venit ad nos: et sacerdotes in regno Darii Persæ, id est regnante Dario rege Persarum, qui templi inchoationem jussit compleri, ut patuit in Esdra. Filii Levi principes familiarum Leviticarum, scripti in libro Verborum dierum, id est Paralipomenon, ubi primo libro descripti sunt in sua radice, hoc est in patribus suis, non in propriis nominibus: qui manserunt in vita, saltem pro parte, usque ad dies Jonathan pontificis filii Eliasib: ita tamen, quod immediatus pater istius Jonathan fuit Joiada, sicut jam patuit.
paras.en: [[12:22|The Levites|Levitæ]] [[12:22|in the days|in diebus]], that is, in the time of the pontificate, [[12:22|of Eliasib, and Joiada, and Johanan|Eliasib, et Joiada, et Johanan]], who a little before was called Jonathan, [[12:22|and Jeddoa|et Jeddoa]], [[12:22|were recorded|scripti]] as [[12:22|the chiefs of the families|principes familiarum]], that is, they were recorded as the principal men in the Levitical families which took their origin from them: but that record has not come down to us; [[12:22|and the priests in the reign of Darius the Persian|et sacerdotes in regno Darii Persæ]], that is, while Darius king of the Persians reigned, who ordered the temple that had been begun to be completed, as was shown in Esdras[[1 Esd 6:12||]] [the margin gives I Esdr. vi; its verse number is unclear]. [[12:23|The sons of Levi, heads of the families|Filii Levi principes familiarum]] of the Levites [[12:23|were written in the book of Chronicles|scripti in libro Verborum dierum]] [in Latin "the book of the words of the days", the Hebrew name of Paralipomenon], that is, of Paralipomenon, where in the first book they are recorded in their root, that is, in their fathers[[1 Par 6:1||]] [the margin seems to read I Par. vi, 1 et seq.; uncertain], not by their own names: who remained alive, at least in part, [[12:23|even unto the days of Jonathan the son of Eliasib|usque ad dies Jonathan pontificis filii Eliasib]] the high priest: yet so that the immediate father of this Jonathan was Joiada, as has already been shown.

paras.t: Et principes Levitarum, id est præcipui et nobiliores inter Levitas: Hasebia, et Serebia, etc., et fratres eorum per vices suas, id est juxta suæ successionis ordinem in suo obsequio, ut laudarent Deum, et confiterentur beneficia ejus, ac sua populique peccata, juxta præceptum, id est ordinationem et jussionem David regis, primo libro Paralipomenon scriptam, et observarent æque per ordinem, id est, successive exsequerentur sua officia æqualiter, unusquisque in tempore suo. Mathania, et ceteri qui sequuntur in textu, fuerunt custodes portarum templi et vestibulorum ante portas. Hi, supple, fuerunt, in diebus Joachim pontificis et reliquorum qui in textu ponuntur.
paras.en: [[12:24|Now the chief of the Levites|Et principes Levitarum]], that is, the foremost and noblest among the Levites: [[12:24|Hasebia, Serebia|Hasebia, et Serebia]], etc., [[12:24|and their brethren by their courses|et fratres eorum per vices suas]], that is, according to the order of their succession in their service, [[12:24|to praise|ut laudarent]] God, [[12:24|and to give thanks|et confiterentur]] for his benefits, and to confess their own sins and the people's [the Latin *confiteri* means both to give thanks or praise and to confess], [[12:24|according to the commandment|juxta præceptum]], that is, the ordinance and command, of King [[12:24|David|David]], written in the first book of Paralipomenon[[1 Par 16:4||]], [[12:24|and to wait equally in order|et observarent æque per ordinem]], that is, they were to carry out their offices one after another, equally, each in his own time. [[12:25|Mathania|Mathania]], and the others who follow in the text, [[12:25|were keepers of the gates and of the entrances before the gates|custodes portarum templi et vestibulorum ante portas]]. [[12:26|These|Hi]], understand, were, [[12:26|in the days of Joacim|in diebus Joachim]] the high priest, and of the others who are set down in the text.

paras.t: Sequitur de ipsa murorum et civitatis Jerusalem dedicatione. In dedicatione autem, id est instante dedicatione, atque ad faciendum solenniter dedicationem muri Jerusalem, requisierunt, id est convenire fecerunt, Levitas de omnibus locis suis, ut adducerent eos in Jerusalem.
paras.en: There follows the dedication itself of the walls and of the city of Jerusalem. [[12:27|And at the dedication|In dedicatione autem]], that is, when the dedication was at hand, and in order to hold solemnly the dedication [[12:27|of the wall of Jerusalem|muri Jerusalem]], [[12:27|they sought|requisierunt]], that is, they had them come together, [[12:27|the Levites out of all their places, to bring them to Jerusalem|Levitas de omnibus locis suis, ut adducerent eos in Jerusalem]].

paras.t: Et mundati sunt sacerdotes et Levitæ, et mundaverunt populum et murum. Porro sacerdotum tanquam superiorum purgatio fiebat per corporum et vestium lotionem, per orationes, jejunia, continentiamque ad tempus ab uxorum amplexu, et per adspersionem aquæ lustrationis, ac per sacrificia quædam. Interdum tamen ad purgationem eorum non concurrebant hæc omnia. Levitæ autem faciliori ritu mundabantur, quam sacerdotes, quemadmodum secundo libro Paralipomenon legitur, videlicet per adspersionem aquæ lustrationis, orationes et lotiones et alia quædam; non tamen in omnibus fiebat mundatio uno modo. Sacerdotes vero et Levitæ sanctificabant populum, sacrificando et orando pro ipso, adspergendoque eum aqua præfata: de qua in Numerorum libro scribitur. Murum vero sanctificabant aquæ istius adspersione.
paras.en: [[12:30|And the priests and the Levites were purified|Et mundati sunt sacerdotes et Levitæ]], [[12:30|and they purified the people|et mundaverunt populum]], [[12:30|and the wall|et murum]]. Now the purification of the priests, as the higher order, was done by washing the body and the garments, by prayers, fasts, and abstaining for a time from the embraces of their wives, by sprinkling with the water of lustration, and by certain sacrifices. Sometimes, however, not all of these went together for their purification. But the Levites were purified by an easier rite than the priests, as we read in the second book of Paralipomenon[[2 Par 29:34||]], namely by sprinkling with the water of lustration, by prayers and washings and certain other things; yet the purification was not done in the same way in all. And the priests and Levites sanctified the people by sacrificing and praying for them, and sprinkling them with the water just mentioned, of which it is written in the book of Numbers[[Num 19:1||]]. And they sanctified the wall by sprinkling it with that water.

paras.t: Ascendere autem feci ego Nehemias, cujus sunt verba hæc, principes Juda super murum, et statui duos choros magnos laudantium Deum, divisos ab invicem. Et ierunt ad dexteram super murum, primus chorus, et principes quidam eos sequentes, sicut in textu subjungitur: quos et Esdras dicitur præcessisse, secundum quod infra habetur: Esdras scriba ante eos in porta Fontis. Laudabantque Deum in vasis cantici David, id est in musicis instrumentis, in quibus ordinavit David psalmos et cantica decantari. Et contra eos ascenderunt in gradibus civitatis David. Civitas namque David et templum fuerunt in alto sita, ita quod per gradus ascendebatur ad templum: sicque aliqui ab inferioribus ascendebant usque ad murum obviam venientibus per eumdem.
paras.en: [[12:31|And I made|Ascendere autem feci]], I Nehemias, whose words these are, [[12:31|the princes of Juda go up upon the wall|principes Juda super murum]], [[12:31|and I appointed two great choirs to give praise|et statui duos choros magnos laudantium]] to God, divided from one another. [[12:31|And they went on the right hand upon the wall|Et ierunt ad dexteram super murum]], the first choir, and certain princes following them, as is added in the text: and Esdras is said to have gone before them, according to what is found below: [[12:35|and Esdras the scribe before them at the fountain gate|Esdras scriba ante eos in porta Fontis]]. And they praised God [[12:35|with the musical instruments of David|in vasis cantici David]], that is, on the musical instruments on which David ordained that psalms and canticles be sung[[1 Par 16:4||]][[1 Par 16:42||]][[1 Par 23:5||]] [the margin gives I Par. xvi, 4–6, 42, and a third reference hard to read, perhaps I Par. xxiii, 5]. [[12:36|And they went up over against them by the stairs of the city of David|Et contra eos ascenderunt in gradibus civitatis David]]. For the city of David and the temple stood on high ground, so that one went up to the temple by steps: and so some went up from the lower parts as far as the wall, to meet those coming along it.

paras.t: Et chorus secundus gratiam referentium Deo de reparatione civitatis et murorum ac templi, ibat ex adverso, videlicet circumeundo per partem muri oppositam, quousque sibi invicem obviarent in reditu circa templum; et media pars populi super murum ibat, cum isto secundo psallentium choro, cum quo ivit una pars principum, atque pars populi sequens eos: propter quod dicitur ibi fuisse pars media populi; et super, id est prope, turrim Furnorum, juxta quam dicuntur fuisse fornaces; et usque ad murum Latissimum, id est eam partem muri, quæ spissior fuit, eo quod ex illa parte poterat major impugnatio et periclitatio imminere civitati; et super portam Ephraim, id est juxta portam sic dictam, quia fortassis respexit ad terram et sortem tribus Ephraim, ac juxta ceteras portas, quæ consequenter nominantur in littera, usque ad portam Gregis sitam juxta templum, ut dictum est supra; et steterunt in porta Custodiæ, quæ fuit prope atrium templi. Steteruntque duo chori psallentium in domo Dei, et ego, et dimidia pars magistratuum mecum juxta chorum unum. Et sacerdotes, puta Eliachim pontifex, qui jam vocatus est Joachim, Maasia, et alii qui nominantur in littera. Et immolaverunt victimas magnas.
paras.en: [[12:37|And the second choir of them that gave thanks|Et chorus secundus gratiam referentium]] to God for the repair of the city and the walls and the temple [[12:37|went on the opposite side|ibat ex adverso]], that is, going round by the opposite part of the wall, until they should meet one another on the way back near the temple; [[12:37|and the half of the people upon the wall|et media pars populi super murum]] went with this second choir of singers, with which went one part of the princes, and part of the people following them: and that is why it says that half of the people was there; [[12:37|and upon|et super]], that is, near, [[12:37|the tower of the furnaces|turrim Furnorum]], beside which there are said to have been furnaces; [[12:37|even to the broad wall|et usque ad murum Latissimum]], that is, the part of the wall which was thicker, because a greater attack and danger could threaten the city from that side; [[12:38|And above the gate of Ephraim|et super portam Ephraim]], that is, beside the gate so called, perhaps because it faced the land and lot of the tribe of Ephraim, and beside the other gates which are named next in the text, [[12:38|even to the flock gate|usque ad portam Gregis]], which stood near the temple, as was said above[[3:1||]]; [[12:38|and they stood still in the watch gate|et steterunt in porta Custodiæ]], which was near the court of the temple. [[12:39|And the two choirs of them that gave praise stood still at the house of God, and I and the half of the magistrates with me|Steteruntque duo chori psallentium in domo Dei, et ego, et dimidia pars magistratuum mecum]], beside one of the choirs. [[12:40|And the priests|Et sacerdotes]], for instance [[12:40|Eliachim|Eliachim]] the high priest, who has already been called Joacim, [[12:40|Maasia|Maasia]], and the others who are named in the text. [[12:42|And they sacrificed|Et immolaverunt]] [[12:42|great sacrifices|victimas magnas]].

paras.t: Recensuerunt quoque in die illo viros super gazophylacia thesauri: id est, ordinaverunt et numeraverunt viros fideles pro custodia arcarum seu receptaculorum in quibus colligebantur quæ pro sustentaculo vitæ sacerdotum ac Levitarum offerebantur; ad libamina, id est ad recipiendum ibi liquida offerenda, quæ in usum ministrorum templi venerunt, et ad primitias, quæ sacerdotibus solvebantur, et ad decimas, quæ Levitis; ut introferrent per eos principes civitatis, id est, ut ipsi principes inducerent sacerdotes atque Levitas ad ministrandum in templo, et ad commorandum in ejus circuitu, habita ibi competenti provisione, in decore gratiarum actiones, id est cum devota ac pulchra regratiatione ac laude divina; quia lætatus est Juda, id est populus tribus Juda ac Benjamin, in sacerdotibus et Levitis adstantibus, id est devotione, ornatu et obsequio adstantium sacerdotum ac Levitarum.
paras.en: [[12:43|They appointed also in that day men over the storehouses of the treasure|Recensuerunt quoque in die illo viros super gazophylacia thesauri]]: that is, they appointed and counted out faithful men for the keeping of the chests or storerooms in which were gathered the things offered for the support of the life of the priests and Levites; [[12:43|for the libations|ad libamina]], that is, to receive there the liquids to be offered, which went to the use of the ministers of the temple, [[12:43|and for the firstfruits|et ad primitias]], which were paid to the priests, [[12:43|and for the tithes|et ad decimas]], which were paid to the Levites; [[12:43|that the rulers of the city might bring them in by them|ut introferrent per eos principes civitatis]], that is, that the princes themselves should bring in the priests and Levites to minister in the temple and to dwell round about it, with fitting provision made for them there, [[12:43|in honour of thanksgiving|in decore gratiarum actiones]], that is, with devout and fair thanksgiving and praise of God; [[12:43|for Juda was joyful|quia lætatus est Juda]], that is, the people of the tribes of Juda and Benjamin, [[12:43|in the priests and Levites that assisted|in sacerdotibus et Levitis adstantibus]], that is, in the devotion, the adornment and the service of the priests and Levites who stood by.

paras.t: Et custodierunt observationem Dei sui, id est, præcepta a Deo observari jussa adimpleverunt, et specialiter observationem expiationis, id est purgationis qua se ipsos ac populum purificabant. Oportet enim in primis purificare se ipsum, quoniam caritas incipit a suo subjecto; et in Ecclesiastico scriptum est: Ab immundo quid mundabitur? Et cantores et janitores juxta præceptum David et Salomonis, qui multa ordinaverunt observanda in cultu Dei ac templo, atque in ordine ministrorum; quia in diebus David et Asaph, qui fuit propheta, ab exordio, quo duo chori psallentium ordinati fuerunt a David in tabernaculo Dei, erant principes constituti cantorum in carmine laudantium et confitentium Deo, id est carminibus, psalmis et canticis Deo jugiter decantandis, prout primo libro Paralipomenon diffuse describitur.
paras.en: [[12:44|And they kept the watch of their God|Et custodierunt observationem Dei sui]], that is, they fulfilled the precepts which God commanded to be observed, and especially [[12:44|the observance of expiation|observationem expiationis]], that is, of the purification by which they purified themselves and the people. For one must first of all purify oneself, since charity begins with its own subject; and in Ecclesiasticus it is written: [[Ecclus 34:4|What can be made clean by the unclean?|Ab immundo quid mundabitur]] [[12:44|and the singing men, and the porters|Et cantores et janitores]] [[12:44|according to the commandment of David|juxta præceptum David]] [[12:44|and of Solomon|et Salomonis]], who laid down many things to be observed in the worship of God and in the temple, and in the order of the ministers; [[12:45|For in the days of David and Asaph|quia in diebus David et Asaph]], who was a prophet, [[12:45|from the beginning|ab exordio]], when the two choirs of singers were ordained by David in the tabernacle of God, [[12:45|there were chief singers appointed|erant principes constituti cantorum]] [[12:45|to praise with canticles, and give thanks to God|in carmine laudantium et confitentium Deo]], that is, with songs, psalms and canticles to be sung to God without ceasing, as is described at length in the first book of Paralipomenon[[1 Par 16:1||]].

paras.t: Et sanctificabant Levitas, hoc est, populares aptabant ipsos Levitas ad obsequium, providendo eis necessaria vitæ ad ministrandum pro populo; dando quoque Levitis decimas, ostendebant se eis inferiores. Et Levitæ sanctificabant filios Aaron, id est sacerdotes, quibus se fatebantur inferiores, ac subserviebant in cultu Dei: sicque reddebant ipsos sacerdotes ad divini cultus obsequia aptos et expeditos, sed et pontificibus decimas decimarum suarum solvebant. Loquendo autem de sanctificatione consecrationis, superiores sanctificant eos qui inferiores consistunt, dicente Apostolo: Sine ulla contradictione, quod minus est, a majore benedicitur.
paras.en: [[12:46|and they sanctified the Levites|Et sanctificabant Levitas]], that is, the people fitted the Levites for their service by providing them with the necessities of life, so that they might minister for the people; and by giving the Levites tithes they showed themselves their inferiors. [[12:46|and the Levites sanctified the sons of Aaron|Et Levitæ sanctificabant filios Aaron]], that is, the priests, to whom they owned themselves inferior, and whom they served in the worship of God: and so they made the priests fit and free for the duties of divine worship; and they also paid the high priests the tithes of their tithes. But speaking of the sanctification of consecration, the higher sanctify those who stand lower, as the Apostle says: [[Heb 7:7|without all contradiction, that which is less is blessed by the better|Sine ulla contradictione, quod minus est, a majore benedicitur]].

13.title: Elucidatio capituli tertiidecimi: In die autem illo lectum est in volumine Moysis
13.title_en: Elucidation of the thirteenth chapter: And on that day they read in the book of Moses

paras.t: Ponuntur hic vitia absente Nehemia commissa, et ab eodem reverso correcta.
paras.en: Here are set down the faults committed while Nehemias was away, and corrected by him on his return.

paras.t: In die autem, id est tempore illo, sicut frequenter in Scripturis dies pro tempore sumitur, lectum est in volumine Moysis ab Esdra seu alio scriba, audiente populo, quod non debeant introire Ammonites et Moabites in ecclesiam Dei usque in æternum: intelligendo per ecclesiam atrium mundorum, quia nec ipsi vulgares natione Judæi poterant introire Sancta, id est primam et exteriorem templi partem, sed sacerdotes. Sancta autem sanctorum pontifex tantum intravit. Alii per ecclesiam Dei intelligunt communionem in matrimonio. Illa tamen communio fuit alio præcepto prohibita, ut scilicet cum alienigenis idololatris non sociarent connubia. Eo quod non occurrerunt filiis Israel cum pane et aqua egressis de Ægypto, et conduxerunt adversum eos Balaam ariolum ad maledicendum filiis Israel, hoc est ad dandum consilium quo dejicerentur, ut legitur in Numeris. Istud etenim fecit Balac rex Moab, qui etiam fuit rex Madian. Denique hoc præceptum de Ammonitis et Moabitis non ingressuris ecclesiam Dei, continetur in Deuteronomio.
paras.en: [[13:1|And on that day|In die autem]], that is, at that time (as *day* is often taken for time in the Scriptures), [[13:1|they read in the book of Moses|lectum est in volumine Moysis]], Esdras or another scribe reading, [[13:1|in the hearing of the people|audiente populo]], [[13:1|that the Ammonites and the Moabites should not come in to the church of God for ever|quod non debeant introire Ammonites et Moabites in ecclesiam Dei usque in æternum]] [*ecclesia*, "church", means the assembly]: by the church understanding the court of the clean, since not even Jews of common birth could enter the Holy place, that is, the first and outer part of the temple, but only the priests. And into the Holy of holies the high priest alone entered[[Heb 9:6||]][[Heb 9:7||]]. Others understand by the church of God fellowship in marriage. But that fellowship was forbidden by another precept, namely that they should not join in marriage with foreign idolaters[[Deut 7:3||]]. [[13:2|Because they met not the children of Israel with bread and water|Eo quod non occurrerunt filiis Israel cum pane et aqua]] when they came out of Egypt, [[13:2|and they hired against them Balaam|et conduxerunt adversum eos Balaam]] the soothsayer [[13:2|to curse|ad maledicendum]] the children of Israel, that is, to give the counsel by which they might be brought down, as we read in Numbers[[Num 22:5||]][[Num 22:6||]]. For this was done by Balac king of Moab, who was also king of Madian. Lastly, this precept that the Ammonites and Moabites should not enter the church of God is contained in Deuteronomy[[Deut 23:3||]][[Deut 23:4||]].

paras.t: Factum est autem quum audissent legem, id est præceptum hoc legis, separaverunt omnem alienigenam, id est gentilem idololatram, ab Israel, id est a societate et copula Judæorum. Hoc tamen supra nono capitulo legitur factum Nehemia præsente. Sed, ut infra patebit, ipso absente et reverso ad regem, rursus fuerunt sociata conjugia cum alienigenis. Et super hoc erat Eliasib, id est, pontifici illi commissum fuit prohibere de cetero tale scelus: quod tamen non adimplevit; proximus Tobiæ, id est amicus Tobiæ Ammonitæ, ob causam quæ infra habetur.
paras.en: [[13:3|And it came to pass, when they had heard the law|Factum est autem quum audissent legem]], that is, this precept of the law, [[13:3|that they separated every stranger|separaverunt omnem alienigenam]], that is, every heathen idolater, [[13:3|from Israel|ab Israel]], that is, from the company and union of the Jews. This, however, is read above in the ninth chapter[[9:2||]] as done while Nehemias was present. But, as will be seen below, when he was away and had gone back to the king, marriages with foreigners were made again. [[13:4|And over this thing was Eliasib|Et super hoc erat Eliasib]], that is, it was entrusted to that high priest to forbid such wickedness from then on: which, however, he did not carry out; [[13:4|and was near akin to Tobias|proximus Tobiæ]], that is, a friend of Tobias the Ammonite [*proximus* means both "near of kin" and "neighbour, friend"], for the reason given below[[13:28||]].

paras.t: Fecit ergo sibi iste Eliasib gazophylacium grande, et ibi erant ante eum reponentes, id est, Levitæ et sacerdotes reposuerunt in gazophylacio illo, munera, id est oblationes, et thus et vasa sacra cultus divini, et decimam frumenti, vini et olei, consecrata ad cultum Dei, usumque ministrorum ipsius: et hæc fuerunt inde ex voluntate pontificis hujus amota, et vasa ac thesauri Tobiæ fuerunt ibi repositi.
paras.en: [[13:5|And he made him|Fecit ergo sibi]], this Eliasib, [[13:5|a great storeroom|gazophylacium grande]], [[13:5|where before him they laid up|et ibi erant ante eum reponentes]], that is, the Levites and priests laid up in that storeroom [[13:5|gifts|munera]], that is, offerings, [[13:5|and frankincense, and vessels|et thus et vasa]] sacred to the divine worship, [[13:5|and the tithes of the corn, of the wine, and of the oil|et decimam frumenti, vini et olei]], consecrated to the worship of God and the use of his ministers: and these things were removed from there by the will of this high priest, and the vessels and treasures of Tobias were laid up there.

paras.t: In his autem non fui in Jerusalem: ubi si fuissem, tales abusiones non permisissem. Esdras quoque interim fuit defunctus. Quia anno tricesimo secundo Artaxerxis regis Babylonis, id est regni Babylonis: fuit enim monarcha super regna illa orientalia; veni ad regem, juxta tempus condictum; et in fine dierum, id est circa finem dierum vitæ meæ, vel regis aut servitutis quam regi exhibui, rogavi regem, ut permitteret me ad Judæam et Jerusalem redire. Et de ejus licentia veni in Jerusalem, et intellexi malum, id est peccatum, quod fecerat Eliasib Tobiæ, id est ad complacendum Tobiæ, seu quasi ad commodum ejus, ut faceret ei, puta Tobiæ, thesauros, id est, præberet ei repositoria thesaurorum suorum, in vestibulis domus Dei. Et malum mihi visum est valde, quod scilicet sacrum locum deputavit usui hominis idololatræ seu gentilis; et projeci vasa domus Tobiæ, faciendo ea efferri foras de gazophylacio memorato; præcepique ministris templi, et emundaverunt gazophylacium, forsan adspersione aquæ lustrationis, quoniam ex prætacto abusu fuit contaminatum. Et retuli ibi vasa domus Domini, sacrificium et thus.
paras.en: [[13:6|But in all this time I was not in Jerusalem|In his autem non fui in Jerusalem]]: had I been there, I would not have allowed such abuses. Esdras too had died in the meantime. [[13:6|because in the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon|Quia anno tricesimo secundo Artaxerxis regis Babylonis]], that is, of the kingdom of Babylon: for he was monarch over those eastern kingdoms; [[13:6|I went to the king|veni ad regem]], at the time agreed; [[13:6|and after certain days|et in fine dierum]] [literally "at the end of the days"], that is, towards the end of the days of my life, or of the king's, or of the service I rendered the king, [[13:6|I asked the king|rogavi regem]] to let me go back to Judea and Jerusalem. And by his leave [[13:7|I came to Jerusalem|veni in Jerusalem]], [[13:7|and I understood the evil|et intellexi malum]], that is, the sin, [[13:7|that Eliasib had done for Tobias|quod fecerat Eliasib Tobiæ]], that is, to please Tobias, or as it were for his advantage, [[13:7|to make him|ut faceret ei]], that is, Tobias, [[13:7|a storehouse|thesauros]], that is, to give him storerooms for his treasures, [[13:7|in the courts of the house of God|in vestibulis domus Dei]]. [[13:8|And it seemed to me exceeding evil|Et malum mihi visum est valde]], namely that he had given over a sacred place to the use of an idolatrous or heathen man; and [[13:8|I cast forth the vessels of the house of Tobias|projeci vasa domus Tobiæ]], having them carried [[13:8|out of the storehouse|foras de gazophylacio]] mentioned; [[13:9|And I commanded|præcepique]] the ministers of the temple, [[13:9|and they cleansed|et emundaverunt]] the storeroom [the Douay-Rheims has "cleansed again the vessels"; the Latin reads *gazophylacia*, the storerooms], perhaps by sprinkling it with the water of lustration, since it had been defiled by the abuse just described. And I brought back there [[13:9|the vessels of the house of God, the sacrifice, and the frankincense|vasa domus Domini, sacrificium et thus]].

paras.t: Sequitur aliud malum quod Nehemias correxit. Et cognovi quod partes Levitarum non fuissent datæ, id est, quod populus aut pontifex non dedisset Levitis quod eis pro sustentatione vitæ fuerat pro eorum obsequio dandum, et fugisset unusquisque de Levitis in regionem suam, id est ad loca quæ sibi aptiora poterat invenire, vel ad urbes et villas quas habuerunt olim in regno decem tribuum, ad acquirendum necessaria sibi. Et egi causam adversus magistratus, et pontificem, et ejus fautores, et dixi: Quare dereliquimus domum Dei? Modeste loquitur propter dignitatem pontificis, et connumerat se illis reis, ut per hoc ad pœnitentiam compungerentur celerius. Et est sensus: Cur per subtractionem prætactam fecit Levitas et cantores de templo abscedere? Et congregavi eos, id est, Levitas revocavi, et feci eos stare in stationibus, id est locis et officiis suis. Et omnis Juda, id est populus Juda, apportabat decimam frumenti, vini et olei in horrea, pro Levitarum refectione. Et constituimus super horrea, id est, pro custodia horreorum et rerum contentarum in eis ordinavimus, Selemiam sacerdotem et Sadoc, etc., ut congruenter erogarent Levitis recollecta pro eis. Memento mei, Deus, pro hoc, id est merito hujus beneficentiæ meæ, et ne deleas miserationes meas, quas feci in domo Dei mei, id est, non permittas eas privari effectu beatæ remunerationis, nec eas despicias acceptare.
paras.en: There follows another evil which Nehemias corrected. [[13:10|And I perceived that the portions of the Levites had not been given them|Et cognovi quod partes Levitarum non fuissent datæ]], that is, that the people or the high priest had not given the Levites what was to be given them for the support of their life in return for their service, and that the Levites [[13:10|were fled away every man to his own country|et fugisset unusquisque de Levitis in regionem suam]], that is, to the places he could find best suited to him, or to the cities and villages they had once held in the kingdom of the ten tribes, to get themselves the necessities of life. [[13:11|And I pleaded the matter against the magistrates|Et egi causam adversus magistratus]], and the high priest and his supporters, [[13:11|and said: Why have we forsaken the house of God?|et dixi: Quare dereliquimus domum Dei]] He speaks modestly because of the dignity of the high priest, and counts himself among those guilty men, so that by this they might the sooner be moved to repentance. And the sense is: Why, by the withholding just mentioned, were the Levites and singers made to depart from the temple? [[13:11|And I gathered them together|Et congregavi eos]], that is, I called the Levites back, [[13:11|and I made them to stand in their places|et feci eos stare in stationibus]], that is, in their places and offices. [[13:12|And all Juda|Et omnis Juda]], that is, the people of Juda, [[13:12|brought the tithe of the corn, and the wine, and the oil into the storehouses|apportabat decimam frumenti, vini et olei in horrea]], for the feeding of the Levites. [[13:13|And we set over the storehouses|Et constituimus super horrea]], that is, for the keeping of the storehouses and of the things held in them we appointed [[13:13|Selemias the priest|Selemiam sacerdotem]] [[13:13|and Sadoc|et Sadoc]], etc., to pay out duly to the Levites what had been gathered for them. [[13:14|Remember me, O my God, for this thing|Memento mei, Deus, pro hoc]], that is, for the merit of this kindness of mine, [[13:14|and wipe not out my kindnesses, which I have done relating to the house of my God|et ne deleas miserationes meas, quas feci in domo Dei mei]], that is, do not let them be deprived of the effect of blessed reward, nor disdain to accept them.

paras.t: Deinde narrat, qualiter de violatione sabbati reprehenderit eos. In diebus illis vidi in Juda, id est in populo Juda, quosdam calcantes torcularia in sabbato, etc. Et Tyrii, id est viri ex Tyro gentiles, habitaverunt in ea, scilicet in Judæa. Et objurgavi optimates Juda, et dixi eis: Vos additis super iracundiam Israel, id est, taliter transgrediendo meremini ultionem divinam augeri in filiis Israel, et Deum facitis eis magis iratum, quantum ad similitudinem operis. Factum est autem quum quievissent portæ Jerusalem in die sabbati, id est, quum cessassent a motu apertionis, vel merito cessare sic debuissent, videlicet circa vesperam diei sabbatum præcedentis, in qua vespera incepit sabbatum, id est quies, dixi, et clauserunt januas portarum Jerusalem, ne intrent aliqui ad vendendum quidquam sabbati die. Dixi quoque Levitis, ut mundarentur secundum legem: juxta modum in præcedenti articulo introductum. Et pro hoc memento mei, Deus meus, et parce mihi secundum multitudinem miserationum tuarum. Ecce quam humilis oratio fusa a viro tam justo, qui in tot et tantis virtutum operibus misericordiam imploravit, et juxta ejus immensitatem sibi indulgeri expetiit, sciens quod bonis nostris sint multa mala admixta.
paras.en: Next he tells how he rebuked them for breaking the sabbath. [[13:15|In those days I saw in Juda|In diebus illis vidi in Juda]], that is, among the people of Juda, [[13:15|some treading the presses on the sabbath|quosdam calcantes torcularia in sabbato]], etc. [[13:16|Some Tyrians|Et Tyrii]], that is, heathen men from Tyre, [[13:16|also dwelt there|habitaverunt in ea]], namely in Judea. [[13:17|And I rebuked the chief men of Juda, and said to them|Et objurgavi optimates Juda, et dixi eis]]: [[13:18|And you bring more wrath upon Israel|Vos additis super iracundiam Israel]], that is, by transgressing in this way you deserve that God's vengeance be increased upon the children of Israel, and you make God more angry with them, as far as the likeness of the deed goes. [[13:19|And it came to pass, that when the gates of Jerusalem were at rest on the sabbath day|Factum est autem quum quievissent portæ Jerusalem in die sabbati]], that is, when they had ceased from being opened, or rightly ought so to cease, namely towards the evening of the day before the sabbath, on which evening the sabbath, that is, the rest, began, [[13:19|I spoke|dixi]]: [[13:19|and they shut the gates|et clauserunt januas]] of Jerusalem, so that no one should come in to sell anything on the sabbath day. [[13:22|I spoke also to the Levites that they should be purified|Dixi quoque Levitis, ut mundarentur]] according to the law: in the way set out in the preceding article. [[13:22|for this also remember me, O my God|Et pro hoc memento mei, Deus meus]], [[13:22|and spare me according to the multitude of thy tender mercies|et parce mihi secundum multitudinem miserationum tuarum]]. See how humble a prayer was poured out by so just a man, who amid so many and such great works of virtue implored mercy, and asked to be pardoned according to its immensity, knowing that many evils are mixed with our good deeds.

paras.t: Sequitur reprehensio de illicitis conjugiis: In diebus illis vidi Judæos ducentes uxores Azotidas, id est oriundas ex Azoto urbe Philistinorum. Et maledixi eis, zelo justitiæ; vel per modum propheticæ prænuntiationis seu sub conditione, nisi se emendarent; aut certe temporales punitiones eis imprecando, ne in æternum perirent. Et cecidi, id est verberavi, ex eis viros, id est quosdam, et decalvavi, id est dehonestavi, faciendo abradi barbam, capillosve capitis talium transgressorum; sicut rex Ammonitarum abrasit barbam servorum David: quod tunc erat ingens confusio. Constat quoque ex his, quam male servaverint Judæi sua promissa et juramenta sigillis roborata, per quæ promiserunt violationem sabbati et conjugia cum alienigenis, multaque similia evitare, ut patuit supra.
paras.en: There follows the rebuke for unlawful marriages: [[13:23|In those days also I saw Jews that married wives, women of Azotus|In diebus illis vidi Judæos ducentes uxores Azotidas]], that is, women born in Azotus, a city of the Philistines. [[13:25|and laid my curse upon them|Et maledixi]], out of zeal for justice; or by way of prophetic foretelling, or under a condition, unless they amended; or at any rate calling down temporal punishments on them, so that they might not perish for ever. [[13:25|And I beat|Et cecidi]], that is, struck, [[13:25|some of them|ex eis viros]], that is, certain men, [[13:25|and shaved off their hair|et decalvavi]], that is, put them to shame, by having the beard or the hair of the head of such transgressors shaved off; as the king of the Ammonites shaved off the beards of David's servants[[2 Kings 10:4||]]: which was then a very great disgrace. It is plain too from this how badly the Jews kept their promises and oaths confirmed with seals[[9:38||]], by which they promised to avoid breaking the sabbath and marrying foreigners, and many like things, as was shown above.

paras.t: Deinceps per exemplum ostendit, quam periculosa erant Judæis conjugia talia, eo quod sapientissimus Salomon per ea ad lapsum devenerit, sicut in textu, qui planus est, recitatur. Et dilectus Deo suo erat. Nam nato eo, Dominus jussit eum vocari, Amabilem Domino. Qualiter autem dilexerit eum, super secundo Regum tractatum est. Et posuit eum regem privilegio speciali, non jure primogenituræ. De filiis autem Joiada, id est unus filiorum Joiada, filii Eliasib sacerdotis magni, id est pontificis, qui fuit avus illius filii Joiada, erat Sanaballat gener, id est, filiam ipsius Sanaballat duxit uxorem: ideo Eliasib fecit Tobiæ ea quæ dicta sunt, tanquam amicus ipsius propter Sanaballat, qui familiarissimus erat Tobiæ; quem filium Joiada, fugavi a me tanquam rebellem, quia uxorem illam sacrilegam dimittere recusavit. Recordare, Domine Deus meus, adversum eos qui polluunt sacerdotium: id est, per justam castigationem in vita hac, ostende te memorem iniquitatis ipsorum, qui sacerdotium et sui officii dignitatem ac privilegium inhonorant, ac per hoc tibi ingrati sunt. Ad sacerdotes autem illos legales pertinuit connubia specialiter honesta contrahere, ut patet Levitici vicesimo primo.
paras.en: Next he shows by an example how dangerous such marriages were for the Jews, since the most wise Solomon came to his fall through them[[3 Kings 11:1||]][[3 Kings 11:3||]], as is told in the text, which is plain. [[13:26|and he was beloved of his God|Et dilectus Deo suo erat]]. For when he was born, the Lord bade him be called [[2 Kings 12:25|Amiable to the Lord|Amabilem Domino]]. And how He loved him was treated in the second book of Kings[[2 Kings 12:24||]]. [[13:26|and God made him king|Et posuit eum regem]] by a special privilege, not by right of the firstborn. [[13:28|And one of the sons of Joiada|De filiis autem Joiada]], that is, one of the sons of Joiada, [[13:28|the son of Eliasib the high priest|filii Eliasib sacerdotis magni]], that is, the pontiff, who was the grandfather of that son of Joiada, [[13:28|was son in law to Sanaballat|erat Sanaballat gener]], that is, he married the daughter of Sanaballat himself: and that is why Eliasib did for Tobias the things that were told[[13:7||]], as being his friend on account of Sanaballat, who was very intimate with Tobias; and as for that son of Joiada, [[13:28|I drove him from me|fugavi a me]] as a rebel, because he refused to put away that sacrilegious wife. [[13:29|Remember them, O Lord my God, that defile the priesthood|Recordare, Domine Deus meus, adversum eos qui polluunt sacerdotium]]: that is, by just chastisement in this life show that thou rememberest the iniquity of those who dishonour the priesthood and the dignity and privilege of their office, and so are ungrateful to thee. For it belonged to those priests of the law to contract marriages of especial honour, as is plain from the twenty-first chapter of Leviticus[[Lev 21:13||]][[Lev 21:14||]].
