paras.t: Igitur mundavi eos ab omnibus alienigenis uxoribus, nisi forsan paucis induratis exceptis; et constitui sacerdotum ordines et Levitarum, unumquemque ordinem in ministerio suo: ut quilibet ordo illorum serviret in tempore suo in templo, quemadmodum primo libro Paralipomenon legitur David fecisse: tempore enim Nehemiæ sacerdotes jam erant multiplicati; et in oblatione et appositione lignorum in ignem perpetuum in altari holocaustorum semper ardentem, quem sacerdotes tenebantur nutrire, ponendo ligna in eo quotidie: ideo additur, temporibus constitutis; et in primitiis, id est in accipiendo primitias, hoc est primos præcipuosque fructus, a populo.
paras.en: [[13:30|So I separated from them all strangers|Igitur mundavi eos ab omnibus alienigenis]] [literally "I cleansed them from all foreign"], that is, from all foreign wives, except perhaps a few hardened ones; [[13:30|and I appointed the courses of the priests and the Levites|et constitui sacerdotum ordines et Levitarum]], [[13:30|every man in his ministry|unumquemque ordinem in ministerio suo]]: so that each of their courses should serve in its own time in the temple, as we read in the first book of Paralipomenon that David did[[1 Par 23:1||]] [the margin gives I Par. xxiii–xxvi]: for by the time of Nehemias the priests had already multiplied; [[13:31|And for the offering|et in oblatione]] and putting [[13:31|of wood|lignorum]] on the perpetual fire, ever burning on the altar of holocausts, which the priests were bound to feed by putting wood on it every day: and so it adds, [[13:31|at times appointed|temporibus constitutis]]; [[13:31|and for the firstfruits|et in primitiis]], that is, in receiving the firstfruits, that is, the first and choicest fruits, from the people.

paras.t: Postremo librum suum in devota et humili oratione concludit, quasi de suis justitiis non præsumens, neque se jactans: Memento, inquiens, mei, Deus meus, in bonum. Quasi dicat: Scio et fateor cum sancto Job, quod universorum memineris; et item, quod quorumdam memor es in malum, hoc est ad debitam ultionem: juxta illud Amos: Juravit Dominus, Si oblitus fuero usque in finem omnia opera eorum. Unde et Salomon contestatur: Cuncta quæ fiunt, adducet Deus in judicium pro omni errato, sive bonum sit, sive malum. Ideo precor, Domine Deus meus, et cum hac oratione tuæ recommendo me pietati. Memento mei, Deus meus, in bonum.
paras.en: Lastly he ends his book with a devout and humble prayer, as one who does not presume upon his own righteous deeds, nor boast: [[13:31|remember|Memento]], he says, [[13:31|me, O my God, unto good|mei, Deus meus, in bonum]]. As if to say: I know and confess with holy Job [[Job 10:13|that thou rememberest all things|quod universorum memineris]]; and again, that thou rememberest some unto evil, that is, unto due vengeance: according to that saying of Amos: [[Amos 8:7|The Lord hath sworn|Juravit Dominus]]: [[Amos 8:7|surely I will never forget all their works|Si oblitus fuero usque in finem omnia opera eorum]] [the Latin keeps the Hebrew form of oath, "if I shall forget"]. And so Solomon too bears witness: [[Eccles 12:14|all things that are done, God will bring into judgment for every error, whether it be good or evil|Cuncta quæ fiunt, adducet Deus in judicium pro omni errato, sive bonum sit, sive malum]]. Therefore I pray, O Lord my God, and with this prayer commend myself to thy loving-kindness: [[13:31|remember me, O my God, unto good|Memento mei, Deus meus, in bonum]].

paras.t: Circa hoc Josephus scribit: Multa talia laudibus digna, dum cum summa fecisset magnificentia Nehemias, ad senectutem perveniens, defunctus est, vir benignus et natura justus, atque circa propriam gentem magnificentissimus, qui in memoria sui æterna muros Jerosolymitanos reliquit. Itaque tam fidelis ac fervidi viri imitemur usque in finem virtutes, et sanctam Dei Ecclesiam jugiter ædificare, roborare, perficere enitamur, pro ea indesinenter orando, exemplariter conversando, et proximos totis viribus adjuvando. Ad laudem et gloriam Omnipotentis, qui est super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: On this Josephus writes: When Nehemias had done many such praiseworthy things with the greatest magnificence, he came to old age and died, a kindly man and just by nature, most generous towards his own nation, who left the walls of Jerusalem as an everlasting memorial of himself[[Ecclus 49:15||]]. Let us therefore imitate to the end the virtues of so faithful and fervent a man, and strive without ceasing to build up, strengthen and perfect the holy Church of God, praying for her unceasingly, living as an example, and helping our neighbours with all our strength. To the praise and glory of the Almighty, who is God over all, most high and blessed. Amen.
